### Task 2.5 - PATCH /api/units/:id: the fenced requirement write

**Goal.** D5 PATCH: when the body touches a requirement key or names a
`landlordId`, each attempt does a consistent unit read (copied, CI-1), decides
"the landlord changes" on that read (the I3 checks move here, CI-5), reads the
landlord of record after the write (CI-4), plans the write (legacy pets
partner, `deposit_conflict` against the merged stored record, the reset then
classification against the NEW landlord, audit fields), and writes through
`updateIfRequirementsCurrent`; a lost condition re-reads and recomputes, at
most 3 attempts, then 409 `property_changed`; a vanished unit answers 404.
So a slow PATCH can never write a map back over a landlord-change REMOVE.
Audit `unit_updated` fields per D13 as ruled in PR1-10 (CI-3): on the fenced
path (a requirement key touched or the landlord changed) only the keys whose
STORED value the write changes; a body re-sending an unchanged landlordId with
no requirement key keeps the plain list. A fenced write that changes NO stored
value still writes (stamps `updated_at`) but appends no `unit_updated` row
(PR1-10a). Every other body keeps today's plain `units.update` and
`Object.keys(validation.fields)`.

- `app/src/routes/units.ts`
- `app/test/unitsApiRequirementsPatch.test.ts` (NEW)

**Step 1 - tests (write first).** Create `app/test/unitsApiRequirementsPatch.test.ts`:

```ts
// property requirements (spec 2026-10-20 D5, D1, D13; plan 2.4): PATCH
// /api/units/:unitId keeps requirement_sources. A body touching a requirement
// key or naming a landlordId reads the unit and its landlord CONSISTENTLY and
// classifies every item whose interpreted value it changes against the
// landlord's CURRENT values (no landlord -> set_here); a landlord change
// REMOVEs the map first and classifies against the NEW landlord. A stored
// legacy pets boolean is rewritten into the new shape with its meaning;
// deposit_conflict is decided against the stored record. The write is fenced
// on the landlordId and map it read: a race re-reads and recomputes, three
// lost races answer 409 property_changed, a vanished unit 404, and a slow
// PATCH never writes its map back over a restore's or a claim's REMOVE.
// requirement_sources is asserted on the HTTP response.
import { describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';
import {
  getUnit,
  patchUnit,
  REQ_STAMP,
  seedLandlord,
  seedUnit,
  unitUpdatedEvents,
} from './helpers/requirementsFixtures.js';
import { makeWebhookHarness, type FakeWorld } from './helpers/twilioWebhookHarness.js';

const LANDLORD_FACTS = { caseworker: false, landlordTyped: true, autoPrimaryEligible: true };

function auditFieldsOf(world: FakeWorld, index = 0): unknown {
  return unitUpdatedEvents(world)[index]?.payload?.['fields'];
}

describe('PATCH /api/units/:id - where each requirement value came from (D5)', () => {
  it('an edit that makes an item differ is set here; editing it back to the landlord value makes it a copy again', async () => {
    const { app, world } = makeWebhookHarness();
    seedLandlord(world, 'c-ll', { req_income_requirements: '3x rent' });
    seedUnit(world, 'u-1');
    const differ = await patchUnit(app, 'u-1', { income_requirements: '2.5x rent' });
    expect(differ.status).toBe(200);
    expect(differ.body.unit.requirement_sources).toEqual({ income_requirements: 'set_here' });
    const back = await patchUnit(app, 'u-1', { income_requirements: '3x rent' });
    expect(back.status).toBe(200);
    expect(back.body.unit.requirement_sources).toEqual({ income_requirements: 'copied' });
    expect((await getUnit(app, 'u-1')).body.unit.requirement_sources).toEqual({ income_requirements: 'copied' });
    expect(auditFieldsOf(world, 0)).toEqual(['income_requirements']);
    expect(auditFieldsOf(world, 1)).toEqual(['income_requirements']);
  });

  it('a PATCH of one Deposit key classifies the whole Deposit item', async () => {

  it('audit fields: a key re-sent with its stored value is not listed (D13, PR1-10)', async () => {

  it('every key re-sent unchanged on the fenced path: 200, updated_at stamped, but no unit_updated row (PR1-10a)', async () => {
    const { app, world } = makeWebhookHarness();

    const res = await patchUnit(app, 'u-1', { beds: 2, income_requirements: '3x rent' });
    expect(res.status).toBe(200);

    expect(res.body.unit.updated_at).not.toBe(REQ_STAMP);

  it('deposit_conflict is decided against the STORED record; sending the amount as null in the same save clears it', async () => {

    expect(unitUpdatedEvents(world)).toHaveLength(0);
    const ok = await patchUnit(app, 'u-1', { deposit_one_month: true, deposit: null });
    expect(ok.status).toBe(200);
    expect(ok.body.unit.deposit_one_month).toBe(true);
    expect(ok.body.unit).not.toHaveProperty('deposit');
    expect(ok.body.unit.requirement_sources).toEqual({ deposit: 'set_here' });
    expect([...(auditFieldsOf(world) as string[])].sort()).toEqual(['deposit', 'deposit_one_month']);

  it('changing landlordId REMOVEs the map', async () => {

    expect(world.units.get('u-1')).not.toHaveProperty('requirement_sources');
    expect(auditFieldsOf(world)).toEqual(['landlordId']);

  it('changing landlordId and touching an item: reset first, then classified against the NEW landlord', async () => {
    const { app, world } = makeWebhookHarness();

  it('a landlord of record whose contact record is gone counts as no landlord (a cleared item is set here, not copied)', async () => {

  it('(PIN) re-saving the stored landlordId with no requirement field keeps the map', async () => {

describe('PATCH /api/units/:id - the requirements fence (D5)', () => {
  it('a map changed under the write: re-read, recompute, write - the racing entry is kept', async () => {
    const { app, world } = makeWebhookHarness();
    seedLandlord(world, 'c-ll', { req_income_requirements: '3x rent' });
    seedUnit(world, 'u-1');
    const fenced = world.unitsRepo.updateIfRequirementsCurrent.bind(world.unitsRepo);
    let calls = 0;
    world.unitsRepo.updateIfRequirementsCurrent = async (read, patch) => {
      calls += 1;
      // Staff B's edit of another item lands between this attempt's read and its write.
      if (calls === 1) world.units.get('u-1')!.requirement_sources = { credit_requirements: 'set_here' };
      return fenced(read, patch);
    };
    const res = await patchUnit(app, 'u-1', { income_requirements: '3x rent' });
    expect(res.status).toBe(200);
    expect(calls).toBe(2);
    expect(res.body.unit.requirement_sources).toEqual({ credit_requirements: 'set_here', income_requirements: 'copied' });
    expect(unitUpdatedEvents(world)).toHaveLength(1);
  });

  it('three lost races: 409 property_changed, nothing of this PATCH written, no audit row', async () => {
    const { app, world } = makeWebhookHarness();
    seedLandlord(world, 'c-ll', { req_income_requirements: '3x rent' });
    seedUnit(world, 'u-1');
    const fenced = world.unitsRepo.updateIfRequirementsCurrent.bind(world.unitsRepo);
    let calls = 0;
    world.unitsRepo.updateIfRequirementsCurrent = async (read, patch) => {
      calls += 1;
      world.units.get('u-1')!.requirement_sources = { credit_requirements: calls % 2 === 1 ? 'set_here' : 'copied' };
      return fenced(read, patch);
    };
    const res = await patchUnit(app, 'u-1', { income_requirements: '3x rent' });
    expect(res.status).toBe(409);
    expect(res.body).toEqual({ error: 'property_changed' });
    expect(calls).toBe(3);
    const stored = world.units.get('u-1');
    expect(stored).not.toHaveProperty('income_requirements');
    expect(stored?.updated_at).toBe(REQ_STAMP);
    expect(unitUpdatedEvents(world)).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  it('the unit vanished under the write: 404 unit_not_found, no audit row', async () => {
    const { app, world } = makeWebhookHarness();
    seedLandlord(world, 'c-ll');
    seedUnit(world, 'u-1');
    const fenced = world.unitsRepo.updateIfRequirementsCurrent.bind(world.unitsRepo);
    world.unitsRepo.updateIfRequirementsCurrent = async (read, patch) => {
      world.units.delete('u-1');
      return fenced(read, patch);
    };
    const res = await patchUnit(app, 'u-1', { income_requirements: '3x rent' });
    expect(res.status).toBe(404);
    expect(res.body).toEqual({ error: 'unit_not_found' });
    expect(world.auditEvents).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  it("a slow PATCH never writes its map back over a roster claim's REMOVE: recomputed against the claimed landlord", async () => {
    const { app, world } = makeWebhookHarness();
    seedLandlord(world, 'c-new', { req_credit_requirements: 'Score 600+' });
    seedUnit(world, 'u-1', {
      landlordId: undefined,
      contacts: [{ contactId: 'c-pm', role: 'pm', primaryContact: true }],
      primary_contact: 'c-pm',
      requirement_sources: { pets: 'set_here' },
    });
    const fenced = world.unitsRepo.updateIfRequirementsCurrent.bind(world.unitsRepo);
    let raced = false;
    world.unitsRepo.updateIfRequirementsCurrent = async (read, patch) => {
      if (!raced) {
        raced = true;
        await world.unitsRepo.addContact('u-1', { contactId: 'c-new', role: 'landlord' }, LANDLORD_FACTS);
      }
      return fenced(read, patch);
    };
    const res = await patchUnit(app, 'u-1', { credit_requirements: 'Score 600+' });
    expect(res.status).toBe(200);
    expect(res.body.unit.landlordId).toBe('c-new');
    expect(res.body.unit.requirement_sources).toEqual({ credit_requirements: 'copied' });
    expect(world.units.get('u-1')?.requirement_sources).toEqual({ credit_requirements: 'copied' });
  });

  it("a slow PATCH never writes its map back over a restore's REMOVE: recomputed against the restored landlord", async () => {
    const { app, world } = makeWebhookHarness();
    seedLandlord(world, 'c-new', { req_pet_fee: '$300' });
    seedUnit(world, 'u-1', {
      landlordId: 'c-old',
      contacts: [
        { contactId: 'c-old', role: 'landlord', primaryContact: false },
        { contactId: 'c-pm', role: 'pm', primaryContact: true },
      ],
      primary_contact: 'c-pm',
      deleted_at: REQ_STAMP,
      requirement_sources: { pets: 'set_here', credit_requirements: 'set_here' },
    });
    const fenced = world.unitsRepo.updateIfRequirementsCurrent.bind(world.unitsRepo);
    let raced = false;
    world.unitsRepo.updateIfRequirementsCurrent = async (read, patch) => {
      if (!raced) {
        raced = true;
        await world.unitsRepo.restoreWithLandlord('u-1', { expectLandlordId: 'c-old', next: { contactId: 'c-new' } });
      }
      return fenced(read, patch);
    };
    const res = await patchUnit(app, 'u-1', { pet_fee: '$300' });
    expect(res.status).toBe(200);
    expect(res.body.unit.landlordId).toBe('c-new');
    expect(res.body.unit.requirement_sources).toEqual({ pets: 'copied' });
  });
});
```

**Step 2 - run RED.**
`npx vitest run test/unitsApiRequirementsPatch.test.ts`
- Every classification case fails on `requirement_sources` (absent: the route
  writes through the plain `units.update`, `units.ts:2233`, which never
  touches the map).
- The two legacy-pets partner cases fail: the plain update writes only
  `pet_fee`, so the stored boolean stays and `no_pets` / `pets: 'Allowed'`
  are missing, and the audit lists only `pet_fee`.

```ts
/** property requirements (spec 2026-10-20 D5): how one fenced PATCH ended (writeFencedPatch). */
type FencedPatchOutcome =
  | { kind: 'written'; unit: UnitItem; auditFields: string[] }
  | { kind: 'not_found' }
  | { kind: 'deposit_conflict' }
  | { kind: 'property_changed' };

/** D5: a fenced PATCH writes at most this many times, then answers 409 property_changed (the roster writes' bound). */
const REQUIREMENTS_WRITE_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3;
```

```ts
    return { kind: 'decided', promote: heir.kind === 'heir' ? heir.contactId : null };
```

```ts
  /**
   * property requirements (spec 2026-10-20 D5): the landlord of record's
   * contact to classify against, read CONSISTENTLY. A missing record or a
   * routing-pointer row (never a contact) counts as no landlord; any existing
   * record counts, whatever its type or state - an unchanged landlordId is
   * never type-checked (caseworker-integrity L2).
   */
  async function readLandlordOfRecord(contactId: string): Promise<ContactItem | undefined> {
    const contact = await contacts.getById(contactId, { consistentRead: true });
    if (contact === undefined || contact.phone_ref === true || contact.email_ref === true) return undefined;
    return contact;
  }

  /**
   * property requirements (spec 2026-10-20 D5; plan 2.4): the PATCH write for
   * a body that touches a requirement key or names a landlordId. Per attempt:
   * a CONSISTENT read of the unit (absent -> not_found), COPIED, so the fence
   * compares against what this attempt read (the API-test fake hands out its
   * live object, which a concurrent write changes in place); whether the
   * landlord changes, decided on that read (caseworker-integrity I3: a CHANGED
   * landlordId must name a contact typed landlord - requireLandlordContact
   * throws its typed errors, which the caller maps; an empty id is
   * landlord_not_found without a read; an unchanged one is never checked,
   * L2); the landlord of record AFTER the write (readLandlordOfRecord); then
   * planRequirementWrite (deposit_conflict, the legacy pets partner, the
   * reset on a landlord change, the classification, the audit fields) and ONE
   * write fenced on the landlordId and requirement_sources read
   * (unitsRepo.updateIfRequirementsCurrent). A lost condition re-reads and
   * recomputes - a vanished unit answers not_found - at most
   * REQUIREMENTS_WRITE_MAX_ATTEMPTS writes, then property_changed. A restore
   * or a roster claim changes landlordId and REMOVEs the map, so a slow PATCH
   * read before either can never write its map back. A concurrent change of
   * the landlord's own values is not fenced (D5 accepts it).
   */
  async function writeFencedPatch(
    unitId: string,
    fields: Record<string, unknown>,
  ): Promise<FencedPatchOutcome> {
    const landlordPatch = typeof fields['landlordId'] === 'string' ? (fields['landlordId'] as string) : undefined;
    for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= REQUIREMENTS_WRITE_MAX_ATTEMPTS; attempt += 1) {
      const stored = await units.getById(unitId, { consistentRead: true });
      if (stored === undefined) return { kind: 'not_found' };
      const read = structuredClone(stored);
      const changedTo =
        landlordPatch !== undefined && landlordPatch !== read.landlordId ? landlordPatch : undefined;
      let landlord: ContactItem | undefined;
      if (changedTo !== undefined) {
        if (changedTo.length === 0) throw new LandlordNotFoundError();
        landlord = await requireLandlordContact(contacts, changedTo);
      } else {
        const ofRecord =
          typeof read.landlordId === 'string' && read.landlordId.length > 0 ? read.landlordId : undefined;
        landlord = ofRecord === undefined ? undefined : await readLandlordOfRecord(ofRecord);
      }
      const plan = planRequirementWrite({ stored: read, fields, landlord, landlordChanged: changedTo !== undefined });
      if (!plan.ok) return { kind: 'deposit_conflict' };
      try {
        const unit = await units.updateIfRequirementsCurrent(read, plan.patch);
        if (attempt > 1) log.info({ unitId, attempts: attempt }, 'unit patch: requirements fence held on a retry');
        // D13 (plan review PR1-10): a write that touches a requirement key or
        // changes the landlord lists the keys whose STORED value it changed
        // (plan.auditFields: from this attempt's read and the final patch). A
        // body with neither - only an unchanged landlordId re-sent beside
        // other fields - keeps the plain path's list, Object.keys(fields).
        const auditFields =
          changedTo !== undefined || touchesRequirements(fields) ? plan.auditFields : Object.keys(fields);
        return { kind: 'written', unit, auditFields };
      } catch (err) {
        if (!(err instanceof ConditionalCheckFailedException)) throw err;
        // The unit changed (or vanished) since this attempt's read: the next
        // attempt's read tells which.
      }
    }
    const last = await units.getById(unitId, { consistentRead: true });
    return last === undefined ? { kind: 'not_found' } : { kind: 'property_changed' };
  }
```

```ts
describe('GET /api/units/:id/activity - the Apply reason (property requirements D13)', () => {
  it("projects unit_updated with reason 'requirements_applied' and the field names", async () => {
    const { app, world } = makeWebhookHarness();
    seedUnit(world, 'u-apply');
    await world.auditRepo.append('units#u-apply', 'unit_updated', {
      actor: TEST_SESSION_USER.userId,
      fields: ['no_pets', 'pet_fee'],
      reason: 'requirements_applied',

    expect(res.status).toBe(200);
    expect(res.body.events[0]).toEqual({
      id: expect.any(String),
      at: expect.any(String),
      type: 'unit_updated',
      actorId: TEST_SESSION_USER.userId,
      fields: ['no_pets', 'pet_fee'],
      reason: 'requirements_applied',
    });
  });

  it('(PIN) keeps any other unit_updated reason OFF the wire', async () => {
    const { app, world } = makeWebhookHarness();
    seedUnit(world, 'u-other-reason');
    await world.auditRepo.append('units#u-other-reason', 'unit_updated', {
      fields: ['beds'],
      reason: 'Owner asked',
    });

    const res = await authedGet(app, '/api/units/u-other-reason/activity');
    expect(res.status).toBe(200);
    expect(res.body.events[0]).toMatchObject({ type: 'unit_updated', fields: ['beds'] });
    expect(res.body.events[0]).not.toHaveProperty('reason');
  });

  it("(PIN) keeps 'requirements_applied' OFF the wire on any other event type", async () => {

    seedUnit(world, 'u-status-applied', { status: 'available' });
    await world.auditRepo.append('units#u-status-applied', 'listing_status_changed', {
      from: 'setup',
      to: 'available',
      source: 'manual',
      reason: 'requirements_applied',
    });

    const res = await authedGet(app, '/api/units/u-status-applied/activity');
    expect(res.status).toBe(200);
    expect(res.body.events[0]).not.toHaveProperty('reason');
  });
});
```

  snapshot when the landlord failed to load. Create and PATCH answer 400
  `{ error: 'deposit_conflict' }`; PATCH answers 409
  `{ error: 'property_changed' }`; neither changes any other body. Saving the
  One-month box with `deposit: null` in the same PATCH is what clears the
  amount.
- **S6 (pages).** Every unit response (GET, list, POST, PATCH, restore,
  contacts add / remove) carries `requirement_sources` as stored, absent when
  never written; after a landlord change it is absent until an item is next
  written.
- **S7 (e2e).** No e2e change is expected from S2 itself. A unit PATCH that
  touches a requirement key or names a `landlordId` now does one more
  consistent unit read and one consistent landlord read per attempt.
- **RULED (PR1-10a).** A fenced PATCH whose every key is re-sent unchanged
  (for example a raw `pets: true` on a unit already holding
  `pets: 'Allowed'`) still writes (stamps `updated_at`, today's semantics) but
  appends NO `unit_updated` row - the tombstone no-op reasoning at
  `units.ts:2122-2129`. Implemented in Task 2.5 step 3f and its
  every-key-unchanged test. S6: such a save shows no Activity line.
- **Plan watch (CI-6).** If the planner prefers to fence on the touched
  items' keys too, the change is local to `updateIfRequirementsFenced` /
  `fencedRequirementsWrite` (one more condition per key) plus 2.1 cases, and
  plan 2.3's doc comment.

## 1. CONTRACT ISSUES (for the planner's ruling)

- **CI-1 Apply route lives in its own module.** Spec section 7 names
  `app/src/routes/contacts.ts` for "the apply route". The draft writes it in a new
  sibling `app/src/routes/contactRequirementsApply.ts`, registered on the SAME
  contacts router by `createContactsRouter` - the caseworker-review precedent
  (`contacts.ts:114` import, `contacts.ts:1196` `registerCaseworkerRoutes(router, ...)`,
  `caseworkerReview.ts:56`). Same mount, same path, same auth; contacts.ts is
  already 2918 lines. Proposed ruling: accept.
- **CI-2 The Apply 400 messages are not bound.** Plan 2.4 binds the 400 CASES
  and only one message (`contact is not a landlord`). The draft defines seven
  messages (Task 3.2, `E_*` constants), and three shape refusals the spec's list
  does not name but a parser needs: a `units` entry without a non-empty string
  `unitId`; a `units` entry whose `ownItems` is missing or not an array (the wire
  shape always carries it, D8); an `expected` value that is not a string, number,
  boolean or null. `false` in `expected` is read as blank (D1). The dashboard
  shows none of them (D8 shows only the two 409s and a generic failure).
  Proposed ruling: accept.
- **CI-3 A repeated item id in `items` is de-duplicated, not refused.** Spec and
  plan are silent (they refuse a repeated UNIT). Proposed ruling: accept.
- **CI-4 Apply's per-unit audit append is best-effort.** Plan 2.4 says "Each
  written unit: audit `unit_updated` ..." without failure semantics. The units
  PATCH awaits its audit (`units.ts:2249-2252`), so a failure there is a 500; in
  a 100-unit loop a 500 after committed writes would lose the report of what was
  applied (spec D8: "the response says which"). The draft follows the
  multi-entity precedent (`services/primaryHandoff.ts:127-137`,
  `contacts.ts:2533-2543`): `log.warn` and carry on, the unit stays in `updated`.
  Proposed ruling: accept.
- **CI-5 A non-conditional write failure mid-run is a 500.** A
  `ConditionalCheckFailedException` from `applyRequirements` is the skip
  `changed_during_apply`; any OTHER error is rethrown (the repo convention,
  `units.ts:2234-2240`), so earlier units stay applied and that response cannot
  list them. The dialog's "fails" path re-reads the landlord and its properties
  (D8), which shows the true state. Proposed ruling: accept; the union in 2.1
  has no reason for it and none is added.
- **CI-6 `applyRequirements` must stamp `updated_at`.** Plan 2.3 says
  `updateIfRequirementsCurrent` stamps `updated_at`; `applyRequirements` is "the
  same fence plus attribute_not_exists(deleted_at)", silent on the stamp. Spec
  D8 requires it ("Each written unit gets `updated_at`"); Task 3.2's first write
  case asserts it. Proposed ruling: 2.3 `applyRequirements` stamps `updated_at`
  (S2 owns it; S3 only tests it through the route).
- **CI-7 "the changed req_ keys" = the req_ keys the body carries.** The
  contacts PATCH audit lists `parsed.changedFields` (`contacts.ts:1997-2001`),
  which is every key the BODY supplied, not a value diff (`contacts.ts:731-737`,
  `757-764` push on presence). The edit form sends only changed keys (D2), so in
  practice these are the changed ones. The draft follows the convention.
  Proposed ruling: accept.
- **CI-8 The seed's demo landlord has ONE property.** The only landlord owning
  several full-profile properties is `contact-landlord-0001` (Marcus Bell;
  cast units at `cast.ts:472,680,736`), but he is a LEAN contact (`lean.ts:42`),
  and giving him requirements would change lean. The draft gives requirements to
  the cast PM-managed owner Delia Okonkwo (`cast.ts:1316-1329`), whose one
  property is the `[2, 3]` unit (`cast.ts:1344-1369`); that one property holds
  the copied, the set-here and the landlord-updated item ("its properties" read
  as one). No new unit is added to the demo world. Proposed ruling: accept.
- **CI-9 The contacts PATCH suggestion snapshot skips `req_` keys.** The loop at
  `contacts.ts:1784-1793` calls `extraction.getSuggestion(contactId, f)` for every
  changed field but `type`, so a landlord save would issue one suggestion Get per
  `req_` key. No suggestion targets a `req_` key; the draft skips them there so
  "a `req_pets` write never touches the AI suggestion path" (plan 2.4) holds
  literally and is testable (`getSuggestion` not called). A one-line change plan
  2.4 does not name. Proposed ruling: accept.

`requirements can only be set on a landlord`; a body carrying a Deposit key is

holds both forms; the audit `contact_updated` lists the `req_` keys; a `req_pets`

Delivers: D2 (landlord storage, one key at a time, landlord-only, audit, create
ignores), D1 (landlord-side kinds incl. checkbox/text/money/tour_type REMOVE,

**Step 1 - tests first.** Create `app/test/landlordRequirementsPatch.test.ts`:

```ts
// property-requirements (spec D2, D1, D5, D13; plan 2.4): a landlord's
// requirements are 15 `req_` keys on its contact, written one key at a time
// through PATCH /api/contacts/:contactId. Landlord-only on the RESULTING type;
// 400 deposit_conflict against a consistent read merged with the body; the
// audit contact_updated lists the req_ keys; never the tenant pets /
// pets_source / AI suggestion path; ignored by contact CREATE; and a landlord
// edit never touches a property. Runs on the shared in-memory world, like
// landlordContactFields.test.ts.
import request from 'supertest';
import { describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';
import type { ContactItem } from '../src/repos/contactsRepo.js';
import type { UnitItem } from '../src/repos/unitsRepo.js';
import { TEST_SESSION_COOKIE, TEST_SESSION_USER } from './helpers/authSession.js';
import { makeWebhookHarness, ORIGIN_SECRET, type FakeWorld } from './helpers/twilioWebhookHarness.js';

const LL = 'c-req-landlord';
const NOT_LANDLORD = { error: 'requirements can only be set on a landlord' };

function seedContact(world: FakeWorld, contactId: string, fields: Partial<ContactItem>): void {
  world.contacts.push({
    contactId,
    status: 'active',
    created_at: '2026-10-01T10:00:00.000Z',
    ...fields,
  } as ContactItem);
}

function patchContact(
  app: import('express').Express,
  contactId: string,
  body: Record<string, unknown>,
) {
  return request(app)
    .patch(`/api/contacts/${contactId}`)
    .set('x-origin-verify', ORIGIN_SECRET)
    .set('cookie', TEST_SESSION_COOKIE)
    .send(body);
}

function storedContact(world: FakeWorld, contactId: string): ContactItem | undefined {
  return world.contacts.find((c) => c.contactId === contactId);
}

/** Only the req_ keys of a contact (a stored item or a wire body). */
function reqKeysOf(contact: Record<string, unknown> | undefined): Record<string, unknown> {
  return Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(contact ?? {}).filter(([key]) => key.startsWith('req_')));
}

/** The `fields` of every contact_updated row for the contact, each sorted. */
function contactUpdatedFields(world: FakeWorld, contactId: string): string[][] {
  return world.auditEvents
    .filter((e) => e.entityKey === `contacts#${contactId}` && e.event_type === 'contact_updated')
    .map((e) => [...((e.payload?.['fields'] as string[] | undefined) ?? [])].sort());
}

describe('PATCH /api/contacts/:contactId - landlord requirement keys (D2)', () => {
  it('stores each key in its D1 kind, and GET returns it', async () => {
    const { app, world } = makeWebhookHarness();
    seedContact(world, LL, { type: 'landlord' });
    const want = {
      req_no_evictions_on_program: true,
      req_credit_requirements: '600+ preferred',
      req_no_pets: true,
      req_pets: 'Service animals only',
      req_pet_fee: '$300 one-time',
      req_deposit: 1500,
      req_deposit_flexible: true,
      req_application_fee: 0,
      req_tour_type: 'landlord_led',
      req_tour_process: 'Text to schedule.',
    };
    const res = await patchContact(app, LL, want);
    expect(res.status).toBe(200);
    expect(reqKeysOf(res.body.contact)).toEqual(want);
    expect(reqKeysOf(storedContact(world, LL))).toEqual(want);
    const got = await request(app)
      .get(`/api/contacts/${LL}`)
      .set('x-origin-verify', ORIGIN_SECRET)
      .set('cookie', TEST_SESSION_COOKIE)
      .expect(200);
    expect(reqKeysOf(got.body.contact)).toEqual(want);
  });

  it('writes one key at a time: a later save leaves the other keys as stored', async () => {
    const { app, world } = makeWebhookHarness();
    seedContact(world, LL, { type: 'landlord', req_no_pets: true, req_pets: 'Service animals only' });
    const res = await patchContact(app, LL, { req_pet_fee: '$250' });
    expect(res.status).toBe(200);
    expect(reqKeysOf(storedContact(world, LL))).toEqual({
      req_no_pets: true,
      req_pets: 'Service animals only',
      req_pet_fee: '$250',
    });
  });

  it('REMOVEs a key: false or null for a checkbox, "" or null for text, null for money, "" for tour type', async () => {
    const { app, world } = makeWebhookHarness();
    seedContact(world, LL, {
      type: 'landlord',
      req_no_pets: true,
      req_deposit_flexible: true,
      req_pets: 'Cats OK',
      req_credit_requirements: '600+',
      req_deposit: 900,
      req_tour_type: 'pm_team',
      req_tour_process: 'Text the PM.',
    });
    const res = await patchContact(app, LL, {
      req_no_pets: false,
      req_deposit_flexible: null,
      req_pets: '',
      req_credit_requirements: null,
      req_deposit: null,
      req_tour_type: '',
      req_tour_process: null,
    });
    expect(res.status).toBe(200);
    expect(reqKeysOf(storedContact(world, LL))).toEqual({});
  });

  it.each<[string, unknown]>([
    ['req_pets', true], // no boolean pets on the landlord side (D2)
    ['req_no_pets', 'yes'],
    ['req_deposit', -5],
    ['req_application_fee', '25'],
    ['req_tour_type', 'walk_in'],
  ])('400s %s = %j and stores nothing', async (key, value) => {
    const { app, world } = makeWebhookHarness();
    seedContact(world, LL, { type: 'landlord' });
    const res = await patchContact(app, LL, { [key]: value });
    expect(res.status).toBe(400);
    expect(String(res.body.error)).toContain(key);
    expect(reqKeysOf(storedContact(world, LL))).toEqual({});
    expect(contactUpdatedFields(world, LL)).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('(PIN) ignores an unknown req_ key like any unknown contact key', async () => {
    const { app, world } = makeWebhookHarness();
    seedContact(world, LL, { type: 'landlord' });
    const ok = await patchContact(app, LL, { company: 'Acme Homes', req_bogus: 'x' });
    expect(ok.status).toBe(200);
    expect(storedContact(world, LL)?.company).toBe('Acme Homes');
    expect('req_bogus' in (storedContact(world, LL) ?? {})).toBe(false);
    const alone = await patchContact(app, LL, { req_bogus: 'x' });
    expect(alone.status).toBe(400);
    expect(alone.body).toEqual({ error: 'no updatable fields supplied' });
  });
});

describe('landlord only - the RESULTING type (D2)', () => {
  it.each(['tenant', 'partner', 'team_member', 'unknown'] as const)(
    '400s on a %s and writes nothing',
    async (type) => {
      const { app, world } = makeWebhookHarness();
      seedContact(world, 'c-other', { type });
      const res = await patchContact(app, 'c-other', { req_credit_requirements: '600+' });
      expect(res.status).toBe(400);
      expect(res.body).toEqual(NOT_LANDLORD);
      expect(reqKeysOf(storedContact(world, 'c-other'))).toEqual({});
      expect(contactUpdatedFields(world, 'c-other')).toEqual([]);
    },
  );

  it('400s when the same body re-types a landlord to tenant - the type stays landlord', async () => {
    const { app, world } = makeWebhookHarness();
    seedContact(world, LL, { type: 'landlord' });
    const res = await patchContact(app, LL, { type: 'tenant', req_pets: 'Cats OK' });
    expect(res.status).toBe(400);
    expect(res.body).toEqual(NOT_LANDLORD);
    expect(storedContact(world, LL)?.type).toBe('landlord');
    expect(reqKeysOf(storedContact(world, LL))).toEqual({});
  });

  it('accepts the keys when the same body re-types a contact TO landlord', async () => {
    const { app, world } = makeWebhookHarness();
    seedContact(world, 'c-new', { type: 'unknown', status: 'needs_review' });
    const res = await patchContact(app, 'c-new', { type: 'landlord', req_pets: 'Cats OK' });
    expect(res.status).toBe(200);
    expect(storedContact(world, 'c-new')?.type).toBe('landlord');
    expect(reqKeysOf(storedContact(world, 'c-new'))).toEqual({ req_pets: 'Cats OK' });
  });

  it('404s an unknown contact', async () => {
    const { app } = makeWebhookHarness();
    const res = await patchContact(app, 'c-nobody', { req_pets: 'Cats OK' });
    expect(res.status).toBe(404);
    expect(res.body).toEqual({ error: 'contact_not_found' });
  });

  it('reads the stored contact CONSISTENTLY when the body carries a req_ key', async () => {
    const { app, world } = makeWebhookHarness();
    seedContact(world, LL, { type: 'landlord' });
    const reads = vi.spyOn(world.contactsRepo, 'getById');
    const res = await patchContact(app, LL, { req_pets: 'Cats OK' });
    expect(res.status).toBe(200);
    expect(reads).toHaveBeenCalledWith(LL, { consistentRead: true });
  });
});

describe('deposit_conflict - one month OR a fixed amount (D1)', () => {
  it('400s a one-month deposit over a stored fixed amount - nothing written', async () => {
    const { app, world } = makeWebhookHarness();
    seedContact(world, LL, { type: 'landlord', req_deposit: 1500 });
    const res = await patchContact(app, LL, { req_deposit_one_month: true });
    expect(res.status).toBe(400);
    expect(res.body).toEqual({ error: 'deposit_conflict' });
    expect(reqKeysOf(storedContact(world, LL))).toEqual({ req_deposit: 1500 });
  });

  it('400s a fixed amount over a stored one-month deposit', async () => {
    const { app, world } = makeWebhookHarness();
    seedContact(world, LL, { type: 'landlord', req_deposit_one_month: true });
    const res = await patchContact(app, LL, { req_deposit: 1200 });
    expect(res.status).toBe(400);
    expect(res.body).toEqual({ error: 'deposit_conflict' });
```

### Task 3.2 - POST /api/contacts/:contactId/requirements/apply

**Goal.** The Apply route of D8: refusals in plan 2.4's order (404, 400 not a
landlord, 400 body, 409 `deposit_conflict`, 409 `requirements_changed`), each
writing nothing; then per unit IN ORDER a consistent read, `planUnitApply`,
`unitsRepo.applyRequirements`, a `ConditionalCheckFailedException` -> skip
`changed_during_apply`; one `unit_updated` audit per written unit with
`{ actor, fields: changedKeys, reason: 'requirements_applied', landlordId }`;
200 `{ updated, skipped }`; at most 100 units per request.

Delivers: D8 server side (all refusals and skip reasons; the 100 cap; a listed
item already equal keeps its `set_here` record; an all-blank landlord's Clears
item against existing values; the pets pair normalized; own values skipped only
when not in `ownItems`), D5 ("Apply: every item whose keys the Apply wrote becomes
`copied`"), D13 (Apply audit, never `requirement_sources` in `fields`), spec
section 4 (Apply stamps `updated_at`), spec section 6 "Apply route".

**Files.**
- `app/test/requirementsApplyApi.test.ts` (NEW)
- `app/src/routes/contactRequirementsApply.ts` (NEW)
- `app/src/routes/contacts.ts` (import + registration)

**Step 1 - tests first.** Create `app/test/requirementsApplyApi.test.ts`:

```ts
// property-requirements (spec D8, D5, D13; plan 2.1 planUnitApply, 2.3
// applyRequirements, 2.4): POST /api/contacts/:contactId/requirements/apply
// copies the landlord's CURRENT values of the listed items onto each listed
// property of record. Refusals (404 / 400 / 409) write nothing; then per unit,
// in request order: a consistent read, the pure plan, one conditional write,
// one unit_updated audit. Runs on the shared in-memory world
// (unitsLandlordOfRecord.test.ts pattern).
import { ConditionalCheckFailedException } from '@aws-sdk/client-dynamodb';
import request from 'supertest';
import { describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';
import { phoneRefId, type ContactItem } from '../src/repos/contactsRepo.js';
import type { UnitItem } from '../src/repos/unitsRepo.js';
import { TEST_SESSION_COOKIE, TEST_SESSION_USER } from './helpers/authSession.js';
import { makeWebhookHarness, ORIGIN_SECRET, type FakeWorld } from './helpers/twilioWebhookHarness.js';

const LL = 'c-apply-landlord';
const OTHER_LL = 'c-apply-other-landlord';
const OLD = '2026-09-01T10:00:00.000Z';

// The route's 400 messages (contactRequirementsApply.ts).
const E_ITEMS = 'items must be a non-empty array of requirement item ids';
const E_EXPECTED = 'expected must hold exactly the listed items, each with exactly its keys';
const E_EXPECTED_VALUE = 'expected values must be a string, a number, a boolean or null';
const E_UNITS = 'units must be a non-empty array of at most 100 properties';
const E_UNIT_ID = 'each entry of units needs a unitId string';
const E_UNIT_REPEAT = 'units must not repeat a unitId';
const E_OWN_ITEMS = 'each entry of units needs ownItems, a list of items from items';

/** The landlord most cases apply from, stored as the contacts PATCH stores it. */
const LANDLORD_REQS: Record<string, unknown> = {
  req_credit_requirements: '600+ preferred',
  req_no_pets: true,
  req_pet_fee: '$300',
};
/** `expected` as the dialog sends it: every key of each listed item, null = blank. */
const EXPECTED_CREDIT = { credit_requirements: { credit_requirements: '600+ preferred' } };
const EXPECTED_PETS = { pets: { no_pets: true, pets: null, pet_fee: '$300' } };
const EXPECTED_BOTH = { ...EXPECTED_CREDIT, ...EXPECTED_PETS };
const EXPECTED_BLANK_DEPOSIT = {
  deposit: { deposit_one_month: null, deposit: null, deposit_flexible: null, deposit_notes: null },
};

type UnitRef = string | { unitId: string; ownItems: string[] };

function seedLandlord(world: FakeWorld, reqs: Record<string, unknown> = LANDLORD_REQS): void {
  world.contacts.push({
    contactId: LL,
    type: 'landlord',
    status: 'active',
    firstName: 'Lena',
    lastName: 'Lord',
    ...reqs,
  } as ContactItem);
}

function seedUnit(world: FakeWorld, unitId: string, fields: Record<string, unknown> = {}): void {
  world.units.set(unitId, {
    unitId,
    landlordId: LL,
    status: 'available',
    created_at: OLD,
    updated_at: OLD,
    ...fields,
  } as UnitItem);
}

function applyBody(items: string[], expected: Record<string, unknown>, units: UnitRef[]): Record<string, unknown> {
  return {
    items,
    expected,
    units: units.map((u) => (typeof u === 'string' ? { unitId: u, ownItems: [] } : u)),
  };
}

function postApply(app: import('express').Express, body: Record<string, unknown>, contactId = LL) {
  return request(app)
    .post(`/api/contacts/${encodeURIComponent(contactId)}/requirements/apply`)
    .set('x-origin-verify', ORIGIN_SECRET)
    .set('cookie', TEST_SESSION_COOKIE)
    .send(body);
}

function unitAudits(world: FakeWorld, unitId?: string): FakeWorld['auditEvents'] {
  return world.auditEvents.filter(
    (e) => e.event_type === 'unit_updated' && (unitId === undefined || e.entityKey === `units#${unitId}`),
  );
}

function sortedFields(e: FakeWorld['auditEvents'][number] | undefined): string[] {
  return [...((e?.payload?.['fields'] as string[] | undefined) ?? [])].sort();
}

function unitOf(world: FakeWorld, unitId: string): UnitItem | undefined {
  return world.units.get(unitId);
}

describe('refusals - each writes nothing', () => {
  it('404 contact_not_found for an unknown contact, before the body is read', async () => {
    const { app, world } = makeWebhookHarness();
    seedUnit(world, 'u-1');
    const res = await postApply(app, { items: [] }, 'c-nobody');
    expect(res.status).toBe(404);
    expect(res.body).toEqual({ error: 'contact_not_found' });
    expect(unitAudits(world)).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('404 for a phone pointer row - a routing record, never a contact', async () => {
    const { app, world } = makeWebhookHarness();
    seedLandlord(world, { ...LANDLORD_REQS, phone: '+15550001111' });
    const pointerId = phoneRefId('+15550001111');
    world.contacts.push({
      contactId: pointerId,
      phone: '+15550001111',
      phone_ref: true,
      phone_ref_owner: LL,
    } as unknown as ContactItem);
    const res = await postApply(app, applyBody(['pets'], EXPECTED_PETS, ['u-1']), pointerId);
    expect(res.status).toBe(404);
    expect(res.body).toEqual({ error: 'contact_not_found' });
  });

  it.each(['tenant', 'partner', 'team_member', 'unknown'] as const)(
    '400 for a %s - contact is not a landlord',
    async (type) => {
      const { app, world } = makeWebhookHarness();
      world.contacts.push({ contactId: 'c-not', type, status: 'active', ...LANDLORD_REQS } as ContactItem);
      seedUnit(world, 'u-1', { landlordId: 'c-not' });
      const res = await postApply(app, applyBody(['pets'], EXPECTED_PETS, ['u-1']), 'c-not');
      expect(res.status).toBe(400);
      expect(res.body).toEqual({ error: 'contact is not a landlord' });
      expect(unitOf(world, 'u-1')?.no_pets).toBeUndefined();
    },
  );

  const HUNDRED_AND_ONE = Array.from({ length: 101 }, (_, i) => `u-none-${i}`);
  it.each<[string, Record<string, unknown>, string]>([
    ['items missing', { expected: EXPECTED_PETS, units: [{ unitId: 'u-1', ownItems: [] }] }, E_ITEMS],
    ['items empty', applyBody([], {}, ['u-1']), E_ITEMS],
    ['items naming an unknown item', applyBody(['pets', 'pet_rent'], { ...EXPECTED_PETS, pet_rent: {} }, ['u-1']), E_ITEMS],
    ['expected missing', { items: ['pets'], units: [{ unitId: 'u-1', ownItems: [] }] }, E_EXPECTED],
    ['expected missing a listed item', applyBody(['credit_requirements', 'pets'], EXPECTED_PETS, ['u-1']), E_EXPECTED],
    ['expected naming an unlisted item', applyBody(['pets'], EXPECTED_BOTH, ['u-1']), E_EXPECTED],
    ['an expected item missing a key', applyBody(['pets'], { pets: { no_pets: true, pets: null } }, ['u-1']), E_EXPECTED],
    [
      'an expected item with an extra key',
      applyBody(['pets'], { pets: { no_pets: true, pets: null, pet_fee: '$300', pet_rent: null } }, ['u-1']),
      E_EXPECTED,
    ],
    ['an expected item that is not an object', applyBody(['pets'], { pets: 'No pets' }, ['u-1']), E_EXPECTED],
    [
      'an expected value that is an object',
      applyBody(['pets'], { pets: { no_pets: true, pets: { text: 'x' }, pet_fee: '$300' } }, ['u-1']),
      E_EXPECTED_VALUE,
    ],
    ['units missing', { items: ['pets'], expected: EXPECTED_PETS }, E_UNITS],
    ['units empty', applyBody(['pets'], EXPECTED_PETS, []), E_UNITS],
    ['units over 100', applyBody(['pets'], EXPECTED_PETS, HUNDRED_AND_ONE), E_UNITS],
    ['a unit without a unitId', { items: ['pets'], expected: EXPECTED_PETS, units: [{ ownItems: [] }] }, E_UNIT_ID],
    ['a repeated unit', applyBody(['pets'], EXPECTED_PETS, ['u-1', 'u-1']), E_UNIT_REPEAT],
    ['a unit without ownItems', { items: ['pets'], expected: EXPECTED_PETS, units: [{ unitId: 'u-1' }] }, E_OWN_ITEMS],

  it('a write whose condition fails is skipped as changed_during_apply, and the run goes on', async () => {
    const { app, world } = makeWebhookHarness();
    seedLandlord(world);
    seedUnit(world, 'u-a');
    seedUnit(world, 'u-b');
    vi.spyOn(world.unitsRepo, 'applyRequirements').mockRejectedValueOnce(
      new ConditionalCheckFailedException({ message: 'raced', $metadata: {} }),
    );
    const res = await postApply(app, applyBody(['pets'], EXPECTED_PETS, ['u-a', 'u-b']));
    expect(res.status).toBe(200);
    expect(res.body).toEqual({ updated: ['u-b'], skipped: [{ unitId: 'u-a', reason: 'changed_during_apply' }] });
    expect(unitOf(world, 'u-a')?.no_pets).toBeUndefined();
    expect(unitAudits(world).map((e) => e.entityKey)).toEqual(['units#u-b']);
  });

  it('an exception set between the read and the write is never overwritten', async () => {
    const { app, world } = makeWebhookHarness();
    seedLandlord(world);
    seedUnit(world, 'u-race');
    // The harness getById is NOT mocked: it hands the route the LIVE stored
    // object (twilioWebhookHarness.ts:2886-2888). A colleague's write then lands
    // on the stored unit after the route's read and before its write: the
    // wrapper mutates the stored unit, then calls the real fenced write with
    // exactly what the route passed. Only a route that fences against its OWN
    // copy of the read (ruling AR6) sees the race; a route passing the live
    // object would compare the mutated unit with itself and overwrite the
    // exception.
    const realApply = world.unitsRepo.applyRequirements.bind(world.unitsRepo);
    let passedRead: UnitItem | undefined;
    vi.spyOn(world.unitsRepo, 'applyRequirements').mockImplementationOnce(async (read, patch) => {
      passedRead = read;
      const live = world.units.get(read.unitId);
      if (live !== undefined) {
        live.pets = 'Dogs OK';
        live.requirement_sources = { pets: 'set_here' };
      }
      return realApply(read, patch);
    });
    const res = await postApply(app, applyBody(['pets'], EXPECTED_PETS, ['u-race']));
    expect(res.status).toBe(200);
    expect(res.body).toEqual({ updated: [], skipped: [{ unitId: 'u-race', reason: 'changed_during_apply' }] });
    expect(passedRead).not.toBe(world.units.get('u-race'));
    expect(unitOf(world, 'u-race')?.pets).toBe('Dogs OK');
    expect(unitOf(world, 'u-race')?.no_pets).toBeUndefined();
    expect(unitOf(world, 'u-race')?.requirement_sources).toEqual({ pets: 'set_here' });
    expect(unitAudits(world)).toEqual([]);
  });
});
```

**Step 2 - run RED.**

```
cd W:\tmp\property-requirements\app
npx vitest run test/requirementsApplyApi.test.ts
```

Every case fails: the route does not exist, so Express answers its default 404
with an empty JSON body - each `status` assertion (200 / 400 / 409) fails, and the
two 404 cases fail on `toEqual({ error: 'contact_not_found' })`. No case is a PIN.

**Step 3 - implementation.**

(a) Create `app/src/routes/contactRequirementsApply.ts`:

```ts
// Apply to properties (property-requirements spec D8; plan 2.4):
//
//   POST /api/contacts/:contactId/requirements/apply
//        { units: [{ unitId, ownItems }], items, expected }
//        -> 200 { updated: string[], skipped: [{ unitId, reason }] }
//
// Registered on the contacts router by createContactsRouter, like the
// caseworker-review routes (routes/caseworkerReview.ts). It copies the
// landlord's CURRENT values of the listed items onto each listed property that
// still has this landlord of record, in request order, ONE conditional write
// per property (unitsRepo.applyRequirements) - never one transaction, so a
// failure part way leaves the earlier properties applied. What each property
// gets is the pure planUnitApply (lib/requirements.ts); this route validates,
// refuses, reads, writes and audits. Refusals write nothing, in this order:
// 404 contact_not_found; 400 contact is not a landlord; 400 the body (items,
// expected, units, ownItems); 409 deposit_conflict; 409 requirements_changed.
// The dashboard owns every sentence; it shows only the two 409s.
import { ConditionalCheckFailedException } from '@aws-sdk/client-dynamodb';
import type { Router } from 'express';
import { mergeContext } from '../lib/context.js';
import type { Logger } from '../lib/logger.js';
import {
  hasDepositConflict,
  isRequirementItemId,
  itemValuesEqual,
  landlordItemValue,
  planUnitApply,
  REQUIREMENT_ITEMS,
  type ApplySkipReason,
  type ItemValue,
  type RequirementItemId,
} from '../lib/requirements.js';
import type { AuthedRequest } from '../middleware/auth.js';
import type { AuditRepo } from '../repos/auditRepo.js';
import type { ContactsRepo } from '../repos/contactsRepo.js';
import type { UnitsRepo } from '../repos/unitsRepo.js';

/** D8: the most properties one request may name (the dialog batches by it). */
const APPLY_UNITS_MAX = 100;

const E_ITEMS = 'items must be a non-empty array of requirement item ids';
const E_EXPECTED = 'expected must hold exactly the listed items, each with exactly its keys';
const E_EXPECTED_VALUE = 'expected values must be a string, a number, a boolean or null';
const E_UNITS = `units must be a non-empty array of at most ${APPLY_UNITS_MAX} properties`;
const E_UNIT_ID = 'each entry of units needs a unitId string';
const E_UNIT_REPEAT = 'units must not repeat a unitId';
const E_OWN_ITEMS = 'each entry of units needs ownItems, a list of items from items';

export interface RequirementsApplyDeps {
  contacts: ContactsRepo;
  units: UnitsRepo;
  audit: AuditRepo;
  logger: Logger;
}

interface ApplyRequirementsRequest {
  items: RequirementItemId[];
  /** Per listed item, the landlord's value as the dialog showed it (unit keys; null = blank). */
  expected: Partial<Record<RequirementItemId, ItemValue>>;
  units: Array<{ unitId: string; ownItems: RequirementItemId[] }>;
}

/** Every unit key of each item, in registry order. */
const KEYS_OF_ITEM = new Map<RequirementItemId, readonly string[]>(
  REQUIREMENT_ITEMS.map((item) => [item.id, item.fields.map((field) => field.key)]),
);

function isPlainObject(value: unknown): value is Record<string, unknown> {
  return typeof value === 'object' && value !== null && !Array.isArray(value);
}

/** Validate the body, in plan 2.4's order: items, expected, units, ownItems. */
function parseApplyRequirementsBody(body: unknown): ApplyRequirementsRequest | { error: string } {
  const b = isPlainObject(body) ? body : {};

  const rawItems = b['items'];
  if (!Array.isArray(rawItems) || rawItems.length === 0 || !rawItems.every(isRequirementItemId)) {
    return { error: E_ITEMS };
  }
  // A repeated item id names the same item: de-duplicated, not refused.
  const items: RequirementItemId[] = [...new Set(rawItems as RequirementItemId[])];
  const listed = new Set<string>(items);

  const rawExpected = b['expected'];
  if (!isPlainObject(rawExpected)) return { error: E_EXPECTED };
  const expectedIds = Object.keys(rawExpected);
  if (expectedIds.length !== items.length || !expectedIds.every((id) => listed.has(id))) {
    return { error: E_EXPECTED };
  }
  const expected: Partial<Record<RequirementItemId, ItemValue>> = {};
  for (const id of items) {
    const raw = rawExpected[id];
    const keys = KEYS_OF_ITEM.get(id) ?? [];
    if (!isPlainObject(raw)) return { error: E_EXPECTED };
    const rawKeys = Object.keys(raw);
    if (rawKeys.length !== keys.length || !keys.every((key) => rawKeys.includes(key))) {
      return { error: E_EXPECTED };
    }
    const value: ItemValue = {};
    for (const key of keys) {
      const v = raw[key];
      if (v === null || v === false) value[key] = null; // D1: false is blank
      else if (v === true || typeof v === 'string' || typeof v === 'number') value[key] = v;
      else return { error: E_EXPECTED_VALUE };
    }
    expected[id] = value;
  }

  const rawUnits = b['units'];
  if (!Array.isArray(rawUnits) || rawUnits.length === 0 || rawUnits.length > APPLY_UNITS_MAX) {
    return { error: E_UNITS };
  }
  const unitIds: string[] = [];
  const seen = new Set<string>();
  for (const entry of rawUnits) {
    const unitId = isPlainObject(entry) ? entry['unitId'] : undefined;
    if (typeof unitId !== 'string' || unitId.length === 0) return { error: E_UNIT_ID };
    if (seen.has(unitId)) return { error: E_UNIT_REPEAT };
    seen.add(unitId);
    unitIds.push(unitId);
  }
  const units: ApplyRequirementsRequest['units'] = [];
  for (const [index, entry] of rawUnits.entries()) {
    const ownItems: unknown = isPlainObject(entry) ? entry['ownItems'] : undefined;
    if (
      !Array.isArray(ownItems)
      || !ownItems.every((id): id is RequirementItemId => typeof id === 'string' && listed.has(id))
    ) {
      return { error: E_OWN_ITEMS };
    }
    units.push({ unitId: unitIds[index] ?? '', ownItems: [...new Set(ownItems)] });
  }
  return { items, expected, units };
}

export function registerRequirementsApplyRoute(router: Router, deps: RequirementsApplyDeps): void {
  const log = deps.logger;

  router.post('/:contactId/requirements/apply', async (req: AuthedRequest, res) => {
    const contactId = String(req.params['contactId'] ?? '');
    mergeContext({ contactId });

    // CONSISTENT: both 409s below are decided against this read. A phone or
    // email pointer is a routing record, never a contact (the PATCH's rule).
    const landlord = await deps.contacts.getById(contactId, { consistentRead: true });
    if (landlord === undefined || landlord.phone_ref === true || landlord.email_ref === true) {
      res.status(404).json({ error: 'contact_not_found' });
      return;
    }
    if (landlord.type !== 'landlord') {
      res.status(400).json({ error: 'contact is not a landlord' });
      return;
    }
    const body = parseApplyRequirementsBody(req.body);
    if ('error' in body) {
      res.status(400).json({ error: body.error });
      return;
    }
    if (hasDepositConflict(landlord, 'landlord')) {
      log.info({ contactId }, 'requirements apply refused: deposit_conflict');
      res.status(409).json({ error: 'deposit_conflict' });
      return;
    }
    // The landlord's CURRENT value of every listed item must equal what the
    // dialog showed (D1 equality), or staff would copy values they never saw.
    const landlordValues: Partial<Record<RequirementItemId, ItemValue>> = {};
    for (const id of body.items) {
      const current = landlordItemValue(landlord, id);
      const shown = body.expected[id];
      if (shown === undefined || !itemValuesEqual(current, shown)) {
        log.info({ contactId, item: id }, 'requirements apply refused: requirements_changed');
        res.status(409).json({ error: 'requirements_changed' });
        return;
      }
      landlordValues[id] = current;
    }

    const actor = req.user?.userId;
    const updated: string[] = [];
    const skipped: Array<{ unitId: string; reason: ApplySkipReason }> = [];
    for (const { unitId, ownItems } of body.units) {
      const raw = await deps.units.getById(unitId, { consistentRead: true });
      // The route's OWN copy of the consistent read (ruling AR6): a repo may
      // hand out its live stored object (the harness does), and the fence must
      // compare the stored unit with what was READ, not with whatever that
      // object has become by the time the write runs.
      const read = raw === undefined ? undefined : structuredClone(raw);
      const plan = planUnitApply({ unit: read, landlordId: contactId, items: body.items, landlordValues, ownItems });
      // planUnitApply skips an unread unit as not_found; the `read` test only
      // narrows the type for the write below.
      if (plan.kind === 'skip' || read === undefined) {
        skipped.push({ unitId, reason: plan.kind === 'skip' ? plan.reason : 'not_found' });
        continue;
      }
      try {
        // Conditioned on the unit still existing, not deleted, with this
        // landlordId and the requirement_sources it was read with (plan 2.3).
        await deps.units.applyRequirements(read, plan.patch);
      } catch (err) {
        if (err instanceof ConditionalCheckFailedException) {
          skipped.push({ unitId, reason: 'changed_during_apply' });
          continue;
        }
        throw err; // Express 5 forwards async throws to the error handler.
      }
      updated.push(unitId);
      // One unit_updated per written unit (D13). Best-effort, like the other
      // multi-entity loops (services/primaryHandoff.ts): the write committed,
      // so a failed audit must not lose the report of what was applied.
      try {
        await deps.audit.append(`units#${unitId}`, 'unit_updated', {
          actor,
          fields: plan.changedKeys,
          reason: 'requirements_applied',
          landlordId: contactId,
        });
      } catch (err) {
        log.warn({ err, contactId, unitId }, 'requirements apply: audit append failed (best-effort)');
      }
    }
    log.info(
      { contactId, items: body.items.length, updated: updated.length, skipped: skipped.length, actor },
      'requirements applied via api',
    );
    res.json({ updated, skipped });
  });
}
```

```ts
// property-requirements (spec section 7 "Seeds", D5, D6): the FULL demo world
// gives ONE landlord requirements - the PM-managed property's owner of record
// (cast persona 10) - and her property holds one item in each display state:
// copied and still equal (no tag), set on this property (purple), and copied
// before the landlord changed it (orange "Landlord updated"). Seeds bypass the
// API, so the seed writes requirement_sources itself. The LEAN e2e world is
// untouched: no contact holds a req_ key and no property holds the map.
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { SEED } from '../src/lib/seed/lean.js';
import { castItems } from '../src/lib/seed/cast.js';
import { matrixItems } from '../src/lib/seed/matrix.js';
import { buildLiveStaticItems } from '../src/lib/seed/live.js';
import {
  hasDepositConflict,
  itemValuesEqual,
  landlordItemValue,
  normalizeRequirementValue,
  parseLandlordRequirementPatch,
  readRequirementSources,
  REQUIREMENT_ITEMS,
  unitItemValue,
} from '../src/lib/requirements.js';

type Row = Record<string, unknown>;
type Tables = Readonly<Record<string, readonly Row[]>>;

// matrix and live are now-relative; a fixed instant makes them deterministic.
const FIXED_NOW = new Date('2026-07-01T12:00:00.000Z');
const OWNER = 'contact-cast-pm-managed-property-owner';
const PM_UNIT = 'unit-cast-pm-managed-property';

const CAST = castItems();
const FULL: readonly Tables[] = [SEED, CAST, matrixItems(FIXED_NOW), buildLiveStaticItems(FIXED_NOW)];

function rowsOf(layers: readonly Tables[], table: string): Row[] {
  return layers.flatMap((tables) => [...(tables[table] ?? [])]);
}

function reqKeysOf(row: Row | undefined): Row {
  return Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(row ?? {}).filter(([key]) => key.startsWith('req_')));
}

const owner = rowsOf([CAST], 'contacts').find((c) => c['contactId'] === OWNER);
const pmUnit = rowsOf([CAST], 'units').find((u) => u['unitId'] === PM_UNIT);

describe('full profile: one demo landlord with requirements', () => {
  it('exactly one contact in the full world holds requirements: the PM-managed property owner', () => {
    const holders = rowsOf(FULL, 'contacts')
      .filter((c) => Object.keys(reqKeysOf(c)).length > 0)
      .map((c) => c['contactId']);
    expect(holders).toEqual([OWNER]);
    expect(owner?.['type']).toBe('landlord');
  });

  it('her requirements are stored exactly as the contacts PATCH would store them', () => {
    const held = reqKeysOf(owner);
    expect(Object.keys(held).sort()).toEqual([
      'req_application_fee',
      'req_credit_requirements',
      'req_deposit_flexible',
      'req_deposit_one_month',
      'req_income_requirements',
      'req_no_evictions_on_program',
      'req_no_pets',
      'req_pets',
      'req_qualifications',
      'req_tour_process',
      'req_tour_type',
    ]);
    expect(parseLandlordRequirementPatch(held)).toEqual({ ok: true, fields: held });
    expect(hasDepositConflict(owner ?? {}, 'landlord')).toBe(false);
  });

  it('her property keeps its two voucher sizes and holds one requirement item in each state', () => {
    expect(pmUnit?.['landlordId']).toBe(OWNER);
    expect(pmUnit?.['voucher_size_accepted']).toEqual([2, 3]);
    const sources = readRequirementSources(pmUnit?.['requirement_sources']);
    // A valid map: the defensive reader drops nothing from it.
    expect(sources).toEqual(pmUnit?.['requirement_sources']);
    expect(sources).toEqual({ credit_requirements: 'copied', pets: 'set_here', income_requirements: 'copied' });
    const equalsLandlord = (id: 'credit_requirements' | 'pets' | 'income_requirements'): boolean =>
      itemValuesEqual(unitItemValue(pmUnit ?? {}, id), landlordItemValue(owner ?? {}, id));
    expect(equalsLandlord('credit_requirements')).toBe(true); // copied, equal: no tag
    expect(equalsLandlord('pets')).toBe(false); // set here: purple "Set on this property"
    expect(equalsLandlord('income_requirements')).toBe(false); // copied, landlord changed: orange
  });

  it("the property's requirement values are what the unit validator would store", () => {
    for (const item of REQUIREMENT_ITEMS) {
      for (const field of item.fields) {
        if (pmUnit === undefined || !(field.key in pmUnit)) continue;
        const value = pmUnit[field.key];
        expect(normalizeRequirementValue(field, value, field.key), field.key).toEqual({ ok: true, value });
      }
    }
  });

  it('no other seeded property holds requirement_sources', () => {
    const holders = rowsOf(FULL, 'units')
      .filter((u) => 'requirement_sources' in u)
      .map((u) => u['unitId']);
    expect(holders).toEqual([PM_UNIT]);
  });
});

describe('lean profile: byte-stable, untouched', () => {
  it('(PIN) no lean contact holds a req_ key and no lean property holds requirement_sources', () => {
    for (const contact of SEED['contacts'] ?? []) expect(reqKeysOf(contact)).toEqual({});
    for (const unit of SEED['units'] ?? []) expect('requirement_sources' in unit).toBe(false);
  });
});
```

## 5. Notes for other slices

- **S1.** S3's tests depend on these behaviors of 2.1: (1)
  `parseLandlordRequirementPatch` error messages NAME the `req_` key (3.1 asserts
  `toContain(key)` for `req_pets: true`, `req_no_pets: 'yes'`, `req_deposit: -5`,
  `req_application_fee: '25'`, `req_tour_type: 'walk_in'`), rejects a boolean
  `req_pets` and a non-boolean checkbox, returns `fields` holding ONLY known `req_`
  keys, and maps `false` / `''` / null to null; (2) `hasDepositConflict(record,
  'landlord')` is true for `req_deposit_one_month: true` plus a numeric
  `req_deposit`; (3) `itemValuesEqual` accepts wire values (`''` and null blank;

  listed; a legacy boolean `pets` that is REMOVEd is), never
  `requirement_sources`; (5) `parseLandlordRequirementPatch(held)` round-trips the
  seed's stored values unchanged (3.3).
- **S2.** (1) `applyRequirements` stamps `updated_at` (CI-6). (2) Per ruling
  AR6 the Apply route passes its OWN `structuredClone` of the consistent read to
  both `planUnitApply` and `applyRequirements` (the harness `getById` hands out
  the LIVE stored object), so the fake `applyRequirements` must compare the
  passed `read`'s `landlordId` and `requirement_sources` against the stored unit
  BY VALUE (absent vs present included). 3.2's race case leaves `getById`
  unmocked, mutates the stored unit inside an `applyRequirements` wrapper, then
  calls the real fake with the route's arguments and expects
  `changed_during_apply`. A `deleted_at: ''` unit is live for both the fake and
  `planUnitApply` (matching `isDeleted`); 3.2 seeds only a non-empty stamp. (3) It must throw a real
  `ConditionalCheckFailedException` (the harness `conditionalCheckFailed` helper,
  `twilioWebhookHarness.ts:625-626`); the route tests `instanceof`. (4) It must
  REMOVE the null keys of the patch and SET the map whole. (5) The Apply audit row
  is `units#<unitId>` / `unit_updated` / `{ actor, fields, reason:
  'requirements_applied', landlordId }`; `toUnitActivityEvent` lifts exactly that
  `reason`.
- **S6 (Apply dialog).** The wire: every `units` entry MUST carry `ownItems` (an
  array, `[]` for none) or the request is 400; `expected` must hold every listed
  item with EVERY key of the item (null for blank). `skipped` comes back in
  request order; `updated` in request order. The server reads the landlord
  CONSISTENTLY and 409s `requirements_changed` on any listed item that differs
  from `expected`, `deposit_conflict` before that. The seven 400 messages are
  caller bugs, never shown. A non-conditional server failure mid-request is a 500
  with no partial report (CI-5): treat it as "failed" (re-read, D8 copy).
- **S6 (landlord form).** The contacts PATCH 400s `deposit_conflict` when the
  body checks One month's rent over a stored amount unless the same body sends
  `req_deposit: null` (D1) - the 3.1 accept case pins the form's save shape.
  Unknown `req_` keys are silently ignored, so a typo in the form's key mapping
  fails quietly; S6's form test should assert the exact PATCH body.
- **S7.** S3 changes no UI and no e2e spec. The PM persona is referenced by no
  e2e spec; the full demo world now shows one property with all three tags
  (`unit-cast-pm-managed-property`, landlord Delia Okonkwo) - useful for self-QA
  in a `full` reseed. GLOSSARY "requirements (landlord and property)" can name
  the `req_` prefix and the Apply route.
- **Accepted, not fenced (informational).** The contacts PATCH
  `deposit_conflict` check is read-then-write (the contacts write has no guard on
  the deposit keys), so two concurrent landlord saves could in theory store both
  forms; Apply would then 409 `deposit_conflict` until a staff save fixes it.
  This matches the spec's "checked against a CONSISTENT read" and D5's accepted
  unfenced landlord race. A soft-deleted landlord is not refused by either route
  (the spec is silent).

## 1. CONTRACT ISSUES (for the planner to rule)

CI-1. `bedroomSizesOfFilter` (plan 2.5) keeps "finite integers" in the list
arm but "a finite legacy bedroomSize" in the legacy arm: the two arms differ,
and neither drops a negative. Evidence: every writer of a stored size
validated an integer 0..12 (`app/src/routes/broadcasts.ts:210-217`), so no
stored row holds a negative or a non-integer. Proposed ruling: BOTH arms keep
integers >= 0 only (`Number.isInteger(n) && n >= 0`, then `min(n, 4)`). It only
hardens the one reader; no stored data changes meaning. The drafts below
implement this ruling (app 4.1, dashboard mirror 4.5) and pin it with the
same cases in both suites.

CI-2. D12 says the composer pre-fills "one chip per accepted size
(`acceptedVoucherSizes`)" but is silent on a size no chip can hold. The
dashboard `acceptedVoucherSizes` returns ANY finite number
(`dashboard/src/routes/listing/listingFormat.ts:103-109`), and a stored
non-integer voucher size is possible under today's write rule (spec section
2; `voucher_size_accepted` is >= 0 "not limited to integers") as is a
non-integer `beds` (`app/src/lib/unitFields.ts:53,171-174`, kind 'number',
>= 0 only). Today such a property makes the composer send `bedroomSize: 2.5`
(`BroadcastComposer.tsx:205,223`), which the server refuses 400
(`broadcasts.ts:213-215`), so every draft for it fails. Proposed ruling: the
pre-fill leaves such a size out (no chip, not named in the note); when
nothing remains there is no size filter and no note. Consequence to accept:
a property whose ONLY recorded size is a non-integer pre-fills no size (it
reaches every size) - visible on screen (no chip pressed, no note), and S5's
form flags the stored value ("Not a valid size, removed when you save").
Alternative the planner may prefer: round down. Task 4.6 implements and pins
"leave it out" (`prefillVoucherChips`, 4.5).

CI-3. The dashboard `UnitItem.voucher_size_accepted` is typed `number`
(`dashboard/src/api/types.ts:2548`) until S5 widens it (plan 2.6), and the
dashboard tsconfig typechecks test files (`dashboard/tsconfig.json`,
`"include": ["src", ...]`). S4's composer tests need a property that records a
LIST. Proposed ruling: S4 keeps to its types.ts boundary and the composer test
builds such a unit through a local helper `withSizes(sizes)` that casts
(`sizes as unknown as number`); the cast still compiles after S5 widens the
type, and S5 may drop it. Alternative: move the one-line widening
`voucher_size_accepted?: number | number[];` into S4 and out of S5.

CI-4. (clarification) "`bedroomSizes` wins when both are sent" (D12, plan
2.5): the drafts read it as "the legacy key is not READ at all while a list is
present" - not validated either, so `{ bedroomSizes: [3], bedroomSize: 'x' }`
is a 201 storing `[3]`, and `{ bedroomSizes: [], bedroomSize: 2 }` stores no
size (an empty list wins, as an empty `housing_authorities` wins over the
legacy string in `authoritiesOfFilter`, `blastAudienceRules.ts:182-204`).
`bedroomSizes: null` reads as absent (as `housing_authorities: null` does,
`broadcasts.ts:186-187`), so the legacy key is then read. Task 4.3 pins all
three. Rule otherwise if a both-keys 400 is wanted (the housing authority
precedent, `broadcasts.ts:188-190`, is a 400 - but the spec chose "wins").

CI-5. (copy) Plan 1.1's pre-fill note is `Pre-filled to the voucher sizes
this property takes: ` + chip labels. For one size it reads "...voucher sizes
this property takes: 2-BR" (plural for one), and today's second sentence
"- change it to reach other sizes." (`AudienceFilters.tsx:192-196`) is
dropped. The labels are the CHIPS, so two sizes on the 4+ chip are named once
("3-BR, 4+ BR" for 3, 6 and 12). The drafts follow the bound text exactly;
confirm, or bind a singular form.

No other conflict found: plan 2.5's names, signatures and wire shapes match
the code they replace; the preview and send re-reads (`broadcasts.ts:1042`,
`:1285`) need no edit (fact F5).

```ts
/** D12: the top voucher size chip. 4 means "4 or more" (the chip reads "4+ BR"). */
export const VOUCHER_CHIP_MAX = 4;

/** D12 - the ONLY reader of a filter's voucher sizes (validation, the
 *  resolver behind the estimate, preview and send, and every projection):
 *  `bedroomSizes` when it is an array (integers >= 0 kept, each
 *  min(n, VOUCHER_CHIP_MAX), de-duplicated, ascending - even when that leaves
 *  it empty), else a legacy integer `bedroomSize` >= 0 as [min(n, 4)], else
 *  []. A stored row is never rewritten; it is read through here. */
export function bedroomSizesOfFilter(
  filter: { bedroomSizes?: unknown; bedroomSize?: unknown } | undefined,
): number[] {
  if (filter === undefined) return [];
  const isSize = (v: unknown): v is number => typeof v === 'number' && Number.isInteger(v) && v >= 0;
  const list: unknown = filter.bedroomSizes;
  if (Array.isArray(list)) {
    const out = new Set<number>();
    for (const raw of list as unknown[]) {
      if (isSize(raw)) out.add(Math.min(raw, VOUCHER_CHIP_MAX));
    }
    return [...out].sort((a, b) => a - b);
  }
  const legacy: unknown = filter.bedroomSize;
  return isSize(legacy) ? [Math.min(legacy, VOUCHER_CHIP_MAX)] : [];
}

/** D12 match: an empty list filters nothing; otherwise the tenant needs a
 *  voucher size that is a listed size below 4, or is 4 or more while the 4
 *  chip is listed. `sizes` must come from bedroomSizesOfFilter. */
export function voucherSizeMatches(sizes: readonly number[], tenantSize: number | undefined): boolean {
  if (sizes.length === 0) return true;
  if (tenantSize === undefined) return false;
  if (tenantSize >= VOUCHER_CHIP_MAX) return sizes.includes(VOUCHER_CHIP_MAX);
  return sizes.includes(tenantSize);
}

```

(`wireAudienceFilter` is NOT changed here - Task 4.3 changes it together with
the route tests that read it.)

```ts
describe('audience resolution - D12: voucher sizes, any-of, the 4 chip is 4 or more', () => {
  const items = [
    tenant({ contactId: 'v0', voucherSize: 0 }),
    tenant({ contactId: 'v1', voucherSize: 1 }),
    tenant({ contactId: 'v2', voucherSize: 2 }),
    tenant({ contactId: 'v3', voucherSize: 3 }),
    tenant({ contactId: 'v4', voucherSize: 4 }),
    tenant({ contactId: 'v5', voucherSize: 5 }),
    tenant({ contactId: 'v6', voucherSize: 6 }),
    tenant({ contactId: 'v12', voucherSize: 12 }),
    tenant({ contactId: 'v-none' }), // no voucherSize
  ];
  const resolveFor = async (filter: AudienceFilter): Promise<string[]> => {
    const resolve = createAudienceResolutionService({ contactsRepo: fakeContacts(items), logger });
    return (await resolve(filter)).contactIds.sort();
  };

  it('a list matches ANY listed size, in memory; a tenant with no voucher size never matches a size filter', async () => {
    expect(await resolveFor({ ...TENANTS, bedroomSizes: [1, 3] })).toEqual(['v1', 'v3']);
  });

  it('a studio (0) is a size like any other', async () => {
    expect(await resolveFor({ ...TENANTS, bedroomSizes: [0] })).toEqual(['v0']);
  });

  it('the 4 chip is 4 OR MORE: 4 through 12 match, 3 does not', async () => {
    expect(await resolveFor({ ...TENANTS, bedroomSizes: [4] })).toEqual(['v12', 'v4', 'v5', 'v6']);
    expect(await resolveFor({ ...TENANTS, bedroomSizes: [2, 4] })).toEqual(['v12', 'v2', 'v4', 'v5', 'v6']);
  });

  it('an empty list, or none, is no size filter: every size and none resolve', async () => {
    const everyone = ['v-none', 'v0', 'v1', 'v12', 'v2', 'v3', 'v4', 'v5', 'v6'];
    expect(await resolveFor({ ...TENANTS, bedroomSizes: [] })).toEqual(everyone);
    expect(await resolveFor(TENANTS)).toEqual(everyone);
  });

  it('LEGACY stored bedroomSize below 4 still matches exactly', async () => {
    expect(await resolveFor({ ...TENANTS, bedroomSize: 2 })).toEqual(['v2']);
  });

  it('LEGACY stored bedroomSize 4 now reaches every holder of 4 or more (broadcast-4plus-exact-match-underreach)', async () => {
    expect(await resolveFor({ ...TENANTS, bedroomSize: 4 })).toEqual(['v12', 'v4', 'v5', 'v6']);
  });

  it('LEGACY stored bedroomSize 5 to 12 (the uncapped pre-fill) reaches every holder of 4 or more (spec section 4)', async () => {
    expect(await resolveFor({ ...TENANTS, bedroomSize: 6 })).toEqual(['v12', 'v4', 'v5', 'v6']);
  });

  it('a list wins over a legacy number on the same row', async () => {
    expect(await resolveFor({ ...TENANTS, bedroomSizes: [3], bedroomSize: 2 })).toEqual(['v3']);
  });

  it('logs the normalized list as bedroomSizesFilter - never the old bedroomSizeFilter', async () => {
    const capture = createLogCapture();
    const resolve = createAudienceResolutionService({
      contactsRepo: fakeContacts(items),
      logger: createLogger({ level: 'info', destination: capture.stream }),
    });
    await resolve({ ...TENANTS, bedroomSizes: [4, 2] });
    await resolve({ ...TENANTS, bedroomSize: 7 });
    const lines = capture.lines.filter((l) => l['msg'] === 'broadcast audience resolved');
    expect(lines.map((l) => l['bedroomSizesFilter'])).toEqual([[2, 4], [4]]);
    for (const line of lines) expect(line).not.toHaveProperty('bedroomSizeFilter');
  });
});
```

```ts
  // --- property-requirements D12: the voucher size LIST. POST accepts
  // bedroomSizes (it wins) or the legacy bedroomSize and stores bedroomSizes,
  // normalized (each min(n, 4), de-duplicated, ascending; omitted when
  // empty). The estimate, preview and no-body send read a stored row of
  // either shape through bedroomSizesOfFilter, the 4 chip reaching every
  // holder of 4 or more, and the row is never rewritten. Every projection
  // answers bedroomSizes and, when there is a size, the compat bedroomSize. --
  describe('property-requirements D12: voucher sizes at create, preview, send and the projections', () => {
    function postFilter(app: import('express').Express, audience_filter: Record<string, unknown>) {
      return request(app)
        .post('/api/broadcasts')
        .set('x-origin-verify', ORIGIN_SECRET)
        .set('cookie', TEST_SESSION_COOKIE)
        .send({ unitId: 'unit-1', body_template: 'hi', audience_filter });
    }

    function act(app: import('express').Express, broadcastId: string, verb: 'preview' | 'send') {
      return request(app)
        .post(`/api/broadcasts/${broadcastId}/${verb}`)
        .set('x-origin-verify', ORIGIN_SECRET)
        .set('cookie', TEST_SESSION_COOKIE)
        .send({});
    }

    function authedGet(app: import('express').Express, path: string) {
      return request(app).get(path).set('x-origin-verify', ORIGIN_SECRET).set('cookie', TEST_SESSION_COOKIE);
    }

    /** A stored filter with no housing authority, carrying either size shape. */
    const storedFilter = (
      sizes: Pick<BroadcastItem['audience_filter'], 'bedroomSizes' | 'bedroomSize'>,
    ): BroadcastItem['audience_filter'] => ({
      contact_type: 'tenant',
      ...sizes,
      excludeOptedOut: true,
      excludeUnreachable: true,
    });

    /** A searching tenant with recorded consent (seedTenant's defaults) and, when given, a voucher size. */
    function sized(contactId: string, voucherSize?: number): void {
      seedTenant(world, { contactId, ...(voucherSize !== undefined && { voucherSize }) } as Partial<ContactItem>);
    }

    const ids = (candidates: Array<{ contactId: string }>): string[] => candidates.map((c) => c.contactId).sort();

    it('POST stores bedroomSizes normalized - clamped to the 4 chip, de-duplicated, ascending - and the 201 echoes it with the compat bedroomSize', async () => {
      seedUnit(world);
      const { app } = makeWebhookHarness({ world });
      const res = await postFilter(app, { contact_type: 'tenant', bedroomSizes: [3, 6, 2, 3, 5] });
      expect(res.status).toBe(201);
      const stored = world.broadcasts.get(res.body.broadcastId)?.audience_filter;
      expect(stored).toEqual(storedFilter({ bedroomSizes: [2, 3, 4] }));
      expect(stored).not.toHaveProperty('bedroomSize');
      expect(res.body.audience_filter).toEqual({ ...storedFilter({ bedroomSizes: [2, 3, 4] }), bedroomSize: 2 });
    });

    it('LEGACY body: bedroomSize n is stored as bedroomSizes [min(n, 4)], never as bedroomSize', async () => {
      seedUnit(world);
      const { app } = makeWebhookHarness({ world });
      const cases: Array<[number, number[]]> = [
        [2, [2]],
        [0, [0]],
        [7, [4]],
      ];
      for (const [given, expected] of cases) {
        const res = await postFilter(app, { contact_type: 'tenant', bedroomSize: given });
        expect(res.status).toBe(201);
        const stored = world.broadcasts.get(res.body.broadcastId)?.audience_filter;
        expect(stored).toEqual(storedFilter({ bedroomSizes: expected }));
        expect(stored).not.toHaveProperty('bedroomSize');
        expect(res.body.audience_filter).toMatchObject({ bedroomSizes: expected, bedroomSize: expected[0] });
      }
    });

    it('both keys: bedroomSizes wins - the legacy number is not read, and a present empty list is no size filter', async () => {
```

The size parse (anchor - `:210-223`):

```ts
  let bedroomSize: number | undefined;
  if (f['bedroomSize'] !== undefined && f['bedroomSize'] !== null) {
    const v = f['bedroomSize'];
    if (typeof v !== 'number' || !Number.isInteger(v) || v < 0 || v > 12) {
      return { error: 'audience_filter.bedroomSize must be an integer 0..12' };
    }
    bedroomSize = v;
  }
  return {
    contact_type: 'tenant',
    ...(housing_authorities.length > 0 && { housing_authorities }),
    ...(bedroomSize !== undefined && { bedroomSize }),
    excludeOptedOut: true,
    excludeUnreachable: true,
  };
```

replace with:

```ts
  // D12 (property-requirements 2026-10-20): the voucher size LIST. A present
  // bedroomSizes wins and the legacy key is then not read (an old open tab
  // sends only bedroomSize; a new one only bedroomSizes). Either is validated
  // as integers 0..12 and normalized by the ONE reader (bedroomSizesOfFilter);
  // an empty result is no size filter - no key is stored.
  const rawSizes = f['bedroomSizes'];
  const rawSize = f['bedroomSize'];
  let bedroomSizes: number[] = [];
  const isSize = (v: unknown): boolean => typeof v === 'number' && Number.isInteger(v) && v >= 0 && v <= 12;
  if (rawSizes !== undefined && rawSizes !== null) {
    if (!Array.isArray(rawSizes) || !(rawSizes as unknown[]).every(isSize)) {
      return { error: 'audience_filter.bedroomSizes must be an array of integers 0..12' };
    }
    bedroomSizes = bedroomSizesOfFilter({ bedroomSizes: rawSizes });
  } else if (rawSize !== undefined && rawSize !== null) {
    if (!isSize(rawSize)) {
      return { error: 'audience_filter.bedroomSize must be an integer 0..12' };
    }
    bedroomSizes = bedroomSizesOfFilter({ bedroomSize: rawSize });
  }
  return {
    contact_type: 'tenant',
    ...(housing_authorities.length > 0 && { housing_authorities }),
    ...(bedroomSizes.length > 0 && { bedroomSizes }),
    excludeOptedOut: true,
    excludeUnreachable: true,
  };
```

to the resolver, which reads through `bedroomSizesOfFilter` (Task 4.2, F5).

`wireAudienceFilter` (3a).
