## 1. CONTRACT ISSUES (for the planner to rule)

CI-1. Plan 2.6 has no client read of "the landlord's properties", which D8's
dialog must re-read on open. The server already answers
`GET /api/units?landlordId=` from the byLandlord GSI, hiding deleted
properties by default (`app/src/routes/units.ts:750-755`,
`app/src/repos/unitsRepo.ts:919-946,1181-1183`), but the dashboard's
`getUnits` / `getAllUnits` take no `landlordId`
(`dashboard/src/api/endpoints.ts:983-997,1428-1445`). The landlord page itself
loads EVERY unit and filters (`dashboard/src/routes/contact/useContactFile.ts:149-158`,
`buildContactFile.ts:18-20`). Proposed ruling: S6 adds an optional
`landlordId` param to `getUnits` and `getAllUnits` (Task 6.10; no new
`request()` call site, so `e2e/performance/mutationCatalog` is unaffected, and
the read happens only when staff open the dialog, never on a page load the
perf harness measures) and the dialog reads `getAllUnits({ landlordId }, signal)`,
still filtering `landlordId === contactId` and not deleted client-side.

CI-2. RULED (AR36: S5's helper names win). The landlord form uses S5's
`dashboard/src/routes/listing/requirementForm.ts` exactly:
`requirementFormValuesFromLandlord(contact)`,
`buildRequirementPatch(initial, current): { ok: true; patch } | { ok: false; error }`
(it already adds `deposit: null` on the save that checks One month's rent) and
`toLandlordPatch(patch)` (prefixes `req_`). Task 6.9's code and tests use
these; an `ok: false` shows its `error` in the form's error line and sends
nothing (a defensive branch with no UI test - ruling PR2-1; it is pinned in
S5 Task 5.3's `requirementForm.test.ts`). (Was: a proposal for `requirementFormValuesFrom` / `requirementPatch`,
withdrawn.)

CI-3. RESOLVED by S5's draft: `RequirementsFields` renders the four group
fieldsets and the fields only (no section heading, no legend). The landlord
form renders the `<fieldset>` whose `<legend>` is `Requirements / Qualifications`
plus `<FlyerLegend audience="landlord" />` (Task 6.9).

CI-4. Plan 2.6 names `ApplyRequirementsBody` / `ApplyRequirementsResult` but not
their fields. S6 assumes the 2.4 wire exactly:
`ApplyRequirementsBody = { units: Array<{ unitId: string; ownItems: RequirementItemId[] }>; items: RequirementItemId[]; expected: Partial<Record<RequirementItemId, ItemValue>> }`
and `ApplyRequirementsResult = { updated: string[]; skipped: Array<{ unitId: string; reason: ApplySkipReason }> }`.
S6 also imports `RequirementItemId`, `RequirementItem`, `RequirementGroup`,
`ItemValue`, `REQUIREMENT_ITEMS`, `unitItemValue`, `landlordItemValue`,
`itemValuesEqual`, `isItemBlank`, `readRequirementSources` and `isOwnValue`
from `dashboard/src/routes/listing/requirements.ts` (the 2.1 names).

CI-5. Copy gap: D8 and 1.1 give copy for a FIRST request answering 409
`requirements_changed` and for a LATER request answering 409 or failing, but
none for the first request failing any other way (network, 5xx, 409
`deposit_conflict`, a 400). Proposed: the dialog re-reads (the server may have
written before the answer was lost) and shows
`Couldn't update the properties. Review the list and press Update again.`
(Task 6.7 `APPLY_FAILED_NOTICE`).

CI-6. Copy: 1.1 gives the stopped message only as
`Updated <N> properties before this stopped. ...` with no singular. S6 uses
the done message's rule (1.1: `Updated 1 property`), so N = 1 reads
`Updated 1 property before this stopped. Review the rest and press Update again.`

CI-7. RULED (AR39): S5 defines `WASHER_DRYER_LABELS` in
`dashboard/src/routes/listing/requirements.ts`; Task 6.2 IMPORTS it (no second
copy in `listingFormat.ts`, no Step 0), and Task 6.6's flyer row reads the
same map. `formatVoucherSizes`, `recordedVoucherSizes` and `washerDryerLabel`
stay S6's, in `listingFormat.ts` (S5's picker summary is its own
`acceptsSummary`, per S5's note).

CI-8. D8 "Otherwise it closes; the landlord page re-reads its properties ...
and shows `Updated N properties`": S6 reads "shows" as the LANDLORD PAGE
(the dialog has closed) and renders the done message as a `role="status"`
block at the top of the Requirements / Qualifications card, kept until the
next Apply opens or the page moves to another contact. Confirm.

CI-9. D8 "takes the landlord contact the dialog last read": S6 hands EVERY
landlord read the dialog makes to the page (`onLandlordRead` -> `setContact`,
`dashboard/src/routes/contact/useContact.ts:51-53`) instead of only at close;
at close the page therefore holds the last read, as the spec asks, and it is
never behind the dialog while it is open. A Cancel after a stopped run also
re-reads the page's properties (some were written). Confirm.

CI-10. Shared primitives the slice must touch, not listed in 2.6: the shared
`Modal` caps every dialog at 30rem (`dashboard/src/routes/contact/Modal.module.css:23`),
too narrow for dialog B's two columns, so Task 6.10 adds `variant: 'wide'`
(56rem; one column below 860px); and `CardAction` has no disabled state
(`dashboard/src/routes/contact/Card.tsx:34-56`) while D8 needs a disabled
Apply with a reason, so Task 6.8 adds `disabled` and `describedBy`. Both are
additive (every existing caller unchanged).

CI-11. D9 "blank ones as `-`": the dashboard's blank marker is `BLANK`
(U+2014, `dashboard/src/routes/contact/Card.tsx:130`), which the property
page's rows already use; the ASCII spec writes it as "-". S6 uses `BLANK` on
both Requirements cards and on the new Property details rows (1.1: "the
page's existing blank marker").

```ts
// --- D6 display (property requirements spec 2026-10-20) --------------------
// Dashboard-only presentation of the registry above: what the property page
// shows for one item against the landlord's CURRENT value, and how one item
// value reads as one line. Nothing here FILLS a property value from the
// landlord (copy only, D5) - the landlord only explains the property's value.

/** D6 display of one item on a property. */
export interface RequirementDisplay {
  tag: 'set_here' | 'landlord_updated' | null;
  /** 'Landlord: <v>' | 'Landlord now: <v>' | null. */
  landlordLine: string | null;
}

/** One item value as one line: its parts joined by '; '; all blank -> 'blank'.
 *  evictions: 'No evictions while on the program', details;
 *  credit / income / qualifications: the text;
 *  pets: 'No pets', details, 'pet fee ' + fee;
 *  deposit: "One month's rent" or '$N', 'flexible', notes;
 *  application_fee: 0 -> 'No application fee', else '$N';
 *  touring: the tour type's dashboard label, tour process.
 *  '$N' is the property page's money format (formatMoney). */
export function formatItemValue(id: RequirementItemId, value: ItemValue): string {
  const parts: string[] = [];
  const add = (part: string | null): void => {
    if (part !== null && part !== '') parts.push(part);
  };
  const text = (key: string): string | null => {
    const v = value[key];
    return typeof v === 'string' && v.trim() !== '' ? v.trim() : null;
  };
  const money = (key: string): string | null => {
    const v = value[key];
    return typeof v === 'number' && Number.isFinite(v) ? formatMoney(v) : null;
  };
  const checked = (key: string): boolean => value[key] === true;
  switch (id) {
    case 'evictions':
      if (checked('no_evictions_on_program')) add('No evictions while on the program');
      add(text('evictions_notes'));
      break;
    case 'credit_requirements':
    case 'income_requirements':
    case 'qualifications':
      add(text(id));
      break;
    case 'pets': {
      if (checked('no_pets')) add('No pets');
      add(text('pets'));
      const fee = text('pet_fee');
      if (fee !== null) add(`pet fee ${fee}`);
      break;
    }
    case 'deposit':
      // "One month's rent" and a fixed amount are alternatives (D1).
      if (checked('deposit_one_month')) add("One month's rent");
      else add(money('deposit'));
      if (checked('deposit_flexible')) add('flexible');
      add(text('deposit_notes'));
      break;
    case 'application_fee':
      add(value['application_fee'] === 0 ? 'No application fee' : money('application_fee'));
      break;
    case 'touring': {
      const type = text('tour_type');
      if (type !== null) {
        const labels = TOUR_TYPE_LABELS as Readonly<Record<string, string | undefined>>;
        add(labels[type] ?? humanize(type));
      }
      add(text('tour_process'));
      break;
    }
  }
  return parts.length > 0 ? parts.join('; ') : 'blank';
}

/** D6, the tag table. `landlord` undefined = the property has no landlord, or
 *  its contact did not load: no tags and no landlord lines. A blank landlord
 *  value prints 'blank' and COUNTS as differing (Cameron, 2026-10-20). An item
 *  never touched (absent from requirement_sources) whose property value is not
 *  blank reads as set on this property. */
export function requirementDisplay(
  unit: UnitItem,
  landlord: Contact | undefined,
  id: RequirementItemId,
): RequirementDisplay {
  if (landlord === undefined) return { tag: null, landlordLine: null };
  const own = unitItemValue(unit, id);
  const theirs = landlordItemValue(landlord, id);
  if (itemValuesEqual(own, theirs)) return { tag: null, landlordLine: null };
  const shown = formatItemValue(id, theirs);
  const source = readRequirementSources(unit['requirement_sources'])[id];
  if (source === 'copied') return { tag: 'landlord_updated', landlordLine: `Landlord now: ${shown}` };
  if (source === 'set_here' || !isItemBlank(own)) {
    return { tag: 'set_here', landlordLine: `Landlord: ${shown}` };
  }
  return { tag: null, landlordLine: `Landlord: ${shown}` };
}

/** True when the landlord holds no requirement at all (every item blank). Reads
 *  only the req_ keys - never the tenant answers (`pets`, `evictions`) that
 *  share the contacts table. */
export function landlordHasNoRequirements(landlord: Contact): boolean {
  return REQUIREMENT_ITEMS.every((item) => isItemBlank(landlordItemValue(landlord, item.id)));
}

/** The items under their group headings, in display order (D1). */
export interface RequirementItemGroup {
  group: RequirementGroup;
  items: RequirementItem[];
}
export function requirementItemsByGroup(): RequirementItemGroup[] {
  const groups: RequirementItemGroup[] = [];
  for (const item of REQUIREMENT_ITEMS) {
    const last = groups[groups.length - 1];
    if (last !== undefined && last.group === item.group) last.items.push(item);
    else groups.push({ group: item.group, items: [item] });
  }
  return groups;
}
```

If S5's file does not already have the types `RequirementGroup` and
`RequirementItem` in scope (they are 2.1 exports, so it should), add them to
its type imports/declarations rather than redeclaring.

```ts
/**
 * D4 (property requirements spec 2026-10-20): the voucher sizes RECORDED on a
 * property - the property page's "Voucher sizes accepted" row and the New /
 * Edit forms - ascending and de-duplicated. NEVER the bedrooms fallback

 * question. Reads a stored list or an older single number; anything else
 * records nothing.
 */
export function recordedVoucherSizes(unit: { voucher_size_accepted?: unknown }): number[] {
  const isSize = (v: unknown): v is number => typeof v === 'number' && Number.isFinite(v);
  const raw = unit.voucher_size_accepted;
  const list = Array.isArray(raw) ? raw.filter(isSize) : isSize(raw) ? [raw] : [];
  return [...new Set(list)].sort((a, b) => a - b);
}

/** D4 copy: "Studio, 2 BR, 3 BR" (0 is Studio); '' when nothing is recorded. */
export function formatVoucherSizes(sizes: readonly number[]): string {
  return sizes.map((n) => (n === 0 ? 'Studio' : `${n} BR`)).join(', ');
}

/** D3: the label of a stored washer / dryer value (S5's WASHER_DRYER_LABELS,
 *  requirements.ts - the one label map, ruling AR39), or null when none is
 *  recorded. */
export function washerDryerLabel(value: unknown): string | null {
  return value === 'hookups' || value === 'included' || value === 'none' ? WASHER_DRYER_LABELS[value] : null;
}
```

```tsx
// Property requirements D6: the Requirements card compares with the landlord
// OF RECORD, so the page re-reads the landlord contact whenever the unit's
// landlordId changes without a reload - a roster claim of the landlord slot or
// a restore with a landlord both answer through setUnit.
describe('useListing - the landlord is re-read when the landlordId changes', () => {
  function answerSlices(): void {
    getAllUnits.mockResolvedValue(UNITS);
    getAllPlacements.mockResolvedValue(CASES);
    getUnitRelated.mockRejectedValue(new ApiError(404, 'x', 'x'));
    getUnitRecipients.mockRejectedValue(new ApiError(404, 'x', 'x'));
    getUnitSimilar.mockRejectedValue(new ApiError(404, 'x', 'x'));
    getUnitActivity.mockRejectedValue(new ApiError(404, 'x', 'x'));
  }

  it('an ownerless property that gains a landlord reads that landlord, once', async () => {
    answerSlices();
    getUnit.mockResolvedValue({ unitId: 'u1', status: 'available' });
    getContact.mockImplementation((id: string) =>
      Promise.resolve({ contactId: id, type: 'landlord', firstName: id } as Contact),
    );
    const { result } = renderHook(() => useListing('u1'));
    await waitFor(() => expect(result.current.status).toBe('ready'));
    expect(getContact).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    expect(result.current.landlord).toBeNull();

    act(() => result.current.setUnit({ unitId: 'u1', status: 'available', landlordId: 'll2' }));
    await waitFor(() => expect(result.current.landlord?.contactId).toBe('ll2'));
    expect(getContact).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    expect(getContact).toHaveBeenCalledWith('ll2', expect.anything());

    // A later write that keeps the same landlord reads nothing new.
    act(() => result.current.setUnit({ unitId: 'u1', status: 'occupied', landlordId: 'll2' }));
    await act(async () => {
      await Promise.resolve();
    });
    expect(getContact).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
  });

  it('a changed landlord replaces the old one; a failed read leaves none and is not retried; a cleared landlord reads nothing', async () => {
    answerSlices();
    getUnit.mockResolvedValue(UNIT); // landlordId ll1
    getContact.mockImplementation((id: string) =>
      id === 'll3'
        ? Promise.reject(new ApiError(500, 'boom', 'x'))
        : Promise.resolve({ contactId: id, type: 'landlord', firstName: id } as Contact),
    );
    const { result } = renderHook(() => useListing('u1'));
    await waitFor(() => expect(result.current.landlord?.contactId).toBe('ll1'));
    expect(getContact).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);

    act(() => result.current.setUnit({ ...UNIT, landlordId: 'll3' }));
    await waitFor(() => expect(getContact).toHaveBeenCalledWith('ll3', expect.anything()));
    await waitFor(() => expect(result.current.landlord).toBeNull());
    await act(async () => {
      await Promise.resolve();
    });
    expect(getContact).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);

    act(() => result.current.setUnit({ unitId: 'u1', status: 'available' }));
    await act(async () => {
      await Promise.resolve();
    });
    expect(result.current.landlord).toBeNull();
    expect(getContact).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
  });
});
```

```ts
  >({
```

(c) In the load effect's `setState({ status: 'ready', unit, landlord, ...`,
replace the line `          landlord,` (the one right after `          unit,`)

(d) Immediately BEFORE the comment line
`  // setUnit (above) applies an updated unit in place without a refetch - the`,
insert:

```ts
  // D6 (property requirements): re-read the landlord whenever the committed
  // unit's landlordId differs from the one the held landlord was read for - a
  // roster claim of the landlord slot or a restore with a landlord answers with
  // the new unit through setUnit, with no reload. A cleared landlordId resolves
  // to null without a request (loadLandlord).
  const committedLandlordId =
    state.forId === unitId && state.status === 'ready' ? state.unit?.landlordId : undefined;
  const landlordStale =
    state.forId === unitId && state.status === 'ready' && state.unit?.landlordId !== state.landlordForId;
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!landlordStale) return;
    const controller = new AbortController();
    const wanted = committedLandlordId;
    void loadLandlord(wanted, controller.signal)
      .then((landlord) => {
        if (controller.signal.aborted) return;
        setState((prev) =>
          prev.forId === unitId && prev.unit?.landlordId === wanted
            ? { ...prev, landlord, landlordForId: wanted }
            : prev,
        );
      })
      .catch(() => {
        /* aborted: a newer landlordId (or another property) superseded this read */
      });
    return () => controller.abort();
  }, [landlordStale, committedLandlordId, unitId]);

```

Step 3 - implementation. Create `PropertyRequirementsCard.tsx`:

```tsx
// PropertyRequirementsCard - the property page's Requirements card (property
// requirements spec 2026-10-20, D6 layout A and D10): the eight requirement
// items in their groups, each with the PROPERTY's own value (copy only, D5 -
// nothing here fills a value from the landlord). When the landlord of record
// is loaded, an item that differs from the landlord's CURRENT value carries
// ONE tag for the whole item - purple "Set on this property" or orange
// "Landlord updated" - and ONE landlord line (requirementDisplay). No landlord,
// or a landlord that did not load: no tags and no lines.
import type { Contact, UnitItem } from '../../api/index.js';
import { BLANK, Card, CardAction } from '../contact/Card.js';
import { contactDisplayName } from '../contact/format.js';
import {
  formatItemValue,
  isItemBlank,
  landlordHasNoRequirements,
  requirementDisplay,
  requirementItemsByGroup,
  unitItemValue,
} from './requirements.js';
import styles from './PropertyRequirementsCard.module.css';

export interface PropertyRequirementsCardProps {
  unit: UnitItem;
  /** The landlord OF RECORD's contact; undefined when the property has no
   *  landlord or the contact did not load. */
  landlord: Contact | undefined;
  /** Opens the property edit form; absent on a deleted property. */
  onEdit?: () => void;
}

const TAG_TEXT = { set_here: 'Set on this property', landlord_updated: 'Landlord updated' } as const;

export function PropertyRequirementsCard({ unit, landlord, onEdit }: PropertyRequirementsCardProps): React.JSX.Element {
  return (
    <Card
      title="Requirements"
      aside={
        onEdit !== undefined ? (
          <CardAction onClick={onEdit} label="Edit property requirements">
            Edit
          </CardAction>
        ) : undefined
      }
    >
      {landlord !== undefined && landlordHasNoRequirements(landlord) ? (
        <p className={styles.note}>
          {`${contactDisplayName(landlord.firstName, landlord.lastName, landlord.phone)} has no requirements recorded yet.`}
        </p>
      ) : null}
      {requirementItemsByGroup().map(({ group, items }) => (
        <div key={group} className={styles.group}>
          <h4 className={styles.groupHeading}>{group}</h4>
          {items.map((item) => {
            const value = unitItemValue(unit, item.id);
            const display = requirementDisplay(unit, landlord, item.id);
            return (
              // One named group per item: a single-item group's heading
              // already names it, so the item label shows only in groups of
              // several (Screening, Move-in costs).
              <div key={item.id} role="group" aria-label={item.label} className={styles.item}>
                {items.length > 1 ? <span className={styles.itemLabel}>{item.label}</span> : null}
                <span className={styles.itemBody}>
                  <span className={styles.value}>{isItemBlank(value) ? BLANK : formatItemValue(item.id, value)}</span>
                  {display.tag !== null ? (
                    <span className={display.tag === 'set_here' ? styles.tagSetHere : styles.tagLandlordUpdated}>
                      {TAG_TEXT[display.tag]}
                    </span>
                  ) : null}
                  {display.landlordLine !== null ? (
                    <span className={styles.landlordLine}>{display.landlordLine}</span>
                  ) : null}
                </span>
              </div>
            );
          })}
        </div>
      ))}
    </Card>
  );
}
```

Create `PropertyRequirementsCard.module.css`:

```css
/* PropertyRequirementsCard - the property page's Requirements card (property
 * requirements D6 layout A). Tokens only. The two tags differ in LIGHTNESS as
 * well as hue (D6): "Set on this property" is a solid dark violet with white
 * text, "Landlord updated" a pale amber with dark amber text - and each
 * carries its words, never color alone. */

.note {
  margin: 0 0 var(--sp-2);
  font-size: var(--fs-sm);
  color: var(--c-text-muted);
}

.group + .group {
  margin-top: var(--sp-2);
}

.groupHeading {
  margin: 0 0 var(--sp-1);
  font-size: var(--fs-xs);
  font-weight: var(--fw-semibold);
  color: var(--c-text-muted);
}

/* The same label/value rhythm as the Card KV rows (Card.module.css .kv). */
.item {
  display: flex;
  gap: var(--sp-2);
  margin: 2px 0;
  font-size: var(--fs-sm);
}

.itemLabel {
  flex: 0 0 auto;
  min-width: 120px;

}

.itemBody {
  display: flex;
  flex-wrap: wrap;
  align-items: baseline;
  gap: var(--sp-1) var(--sp-2);
  min-width: 0;
}

.value {
  color: var(--c-text);
  white-space: pre-line;
  overflow-wrap: anywhere;
}

.tagSetHere,
.tagLandlordUpdated {
  display: inline-block;
  padding: 0 var(--sp-2);

.landlordLine {
  flex-basis: 100%;
  font-size: var(--fs-xs);
  color: var(--c-text-muted);
  overflow-wrap: anywhere;
}
```

with:

```ts
/** The neighborhood line: the AREA alone (D11). Subzone is a staff-only code
 *  and is not in the projection (D3). */
function neighborhood(flyer: Pick<PublicFlyer, 'area'>): string | null {
  return typeof flyer.area === 'string' && flyer.area.trim() !== '' ? flyer.area : null;
}

/** D11: the voucher sizes as one phrase - "studio", "2-bedroom", "2- or
 *  3-bedroom", "studio or 1-bedroom", "1-, 2-, or 3-bedroom". Ascending and
 *  de-duplicated; every number but the last reads "<n>-", the last
 *  "<n>-bedroom"; a studio always reads "studio". Null for none. */
function voucherPhrase(sizes: readonly number[]): string | null {
  const sorted = [...new Set(sizes.filter((n) => Number.isFinite(n)))].sort((a, b) => a - b);
  const words = sorted.map((n, i) => (n === 0 ? 'studio' : i === sorted.length - 1 ? `${n}-bedroom` : `${n}-`));
  if (words.length === 0) return null;
  if (words.length === 1) return words[0] ?? null;
  if (words.length === 2) return `${words[0]} or ${words[1]}`;
  return `${words.slice(0, -1).join(', ')}, or ${words[words.length - 1]}`;
}
```

```ts
/** D11: "No pets", "No pets (<details>)", or the details alone. A legacy stored
 *  boolean reaches the page already interpreted (true -> details "Allowed",
 *  false -> no_pets), so the page reads only the new shape. */
function petsLabel(flyer: Pick<PublicFlyer, 'no_pets' | 'pets'>): string | null {
  const details = textOrNull(flyer.pets);
  if (flyer.no_pets) return details !== null ? `No pets (${details.trim()})` : 'No pets';
  return details;
}

/** D11: "One month's rent" or "$N", then ", flexible / payment plan
 *  available" when flexible; flexible alone reads "Flexible / payment plan
 *  available". Null when none of the three is recorded (the deposit notes are
 *  staff only and never projected). */
function depositLabel(
  flyer: Pick<PublicFlyer, 'deposit_one_month' | 'deposit' | 'deposit_flexible'>,
): string | null {
  const base = flyer.deposit_one_month ? "One month's rent" : flyer.deposit !== null ? `$${flyer.deposit}` : null;
  if (!flyer.deposit_flexible) return base;
  return base !== null ? `${base}, flexible / payment plan available` : 'Flexible / payment plan available';
}

/** D11: "No application fee" for 0, "$N" otherwise; null when not recorded. */
function applicationFeeLabel(fee: number | null): string | null {
  if (fee === null) return null;
  return fee === 0 ? 'No application fee' : `$${fee}`;
}
```

Step 3 - implementation. Create `applyRequirementsModel.ts`:

```ts
// applyRequirementsModel - the pure rules behind "Apply to properties"
// (property requirements spec 2026-10-20, D8 dialog B), kept apart from the
// dialog so each rule is tested on its own: which CHECKED items would change on
// a property (by interpreted value, D1), which of those are the property's OWN
// values (the D6 definition - never what a card happens to display), each
// row's starting state and the hand rules, the request body, the batching and
// the copy. Staff copy says "property" (GLOSSARY).
import type { ApplyRequirementsBody, ApplyRequirementsResult, Contact, UnitItem } from '../../api/index.js';
import {
  REQUIREMENT_ITEMS,
  isItemBlank,
  isOwnValue,
  itemValuesEqual,
  landlordItemValue,
  readRequirementSources,
  unitItemValue,
  type ItemValue,
  type RequirementItemId,
} from '../listing/requirements.js';
import { formatAddress } from './format.js';

/** Mirror of the server's cap on one Apply request (plan 2.4: more than 100
 *  units is a 400). The dialog sends the checked properties in batches of it. */
export const APPLY_BATCH_SIZE = 100;

/** One property row of "Which properties". */
export interface ApplyRow {
  unitId: string;
  /** The CHECKED items whose value would change here, in display order. */
  changes: RequirementItemId[];
  /** The subset of `changes` that is an own value here (D6). */
  own: RequirementItemId[];
  /** Nothing would change: "Already matches", and the row cannot be checked. */
  alreadyMatches: boolean;
}

/** Hand choices by unitId: true = checked by hand, false = unchecked by hand. */
export type HandChoices = ReadonlyMap<string, boolean>;

/** D8: items with a value start checked; blank items start unchecked ("Clears"). */
export function defaultCheckedItems(landlord: Contact): Set<RequirementItemId> {
  return new Set(
    REQUIREMENT_ITEMS.filter((item) => !isItemBlank(landlordItemValue(landlord, item.id))).map((item) => item.id),
  );
}

/** The checked items in display order - the order the request lists them. */
export function orderedItems(checked: ReadonlySet<RequirementItemId>): RequirementItemId[] {
  return REQUIREMENT_ITEMS.map((item) => item.id).filter((id) => checked.has(id));
}

/** Every row, recomputed from the checked items (D8: live). */
export function applyRows(
  units: readonly UnitItem[],
  landlord: Contact,
  checked: ReadonlySet<RequirementItemId>,
): ApplyRow[] {
  const items = orderedItems(checked);
  return units.map((unit) => {
    const sources = readRequirementSources(unit['requirement_sources']);
    const changes = items.filter((id) => !itemValuesEqual(unitItemValue(unit, id), landlordItemValue(landlord, id)));
    const own = changes.filter((id) => isOwnValue(sources, id, unitItemValue(unit, id)));
    return { unitId: unit.unitId, changes, own, alreadyMatches: changes.length === 0 };
  });
}

/** D8 row state: never checked when it already matches; a hand choice wins;
 *  otherwise checked exactly when no changing item is an own value. */
export function rowIsChecked(row: ApplyRow, hand: HandChoices): boolean {
  if (row.alreadyMatches) return false;
  const chosen = hand.get(row.unitId);
  if (chosen !== undefined) return chosen;
  return row.own.length === 0;
}

/** D8, across a left-column change: a row that becomes "Already matches"
 *  drops its hand choice; a row CHECKED by hand drops it (back to the starting
 *  state, which is then unchecked) when the change ADDS an own-value item to
 *  it - staff confirm it again; removing items never resets it; a row
 *  UNCHECKED by hand stays unchecked. */
export function carryHandChoices(
  hand: HandChoices,
  before: readonly ApplyRow[],
  after: readonly ApplyRow[],
): Map<string, boolean> {
  const previous = new Map(before.map((row) => [row.unitId, row]));
  const next = new Map<string, boolean>();
  for (const row of after) {
    const chosen = hand.get(row.unitId);
    if (chosen === undefined || row.alreadyMatches) continue;
    const was = previous.get(row.unitId);
    const gainedOwn = was !== undefined && row.own.some((id) => !was.own.includes(id));
    if (chosen && gainedOwn) continue;
    next.set(row.unitId, chosen);
  }
  return next;
}

/** Split a list into consecutive batches of at most `size`. */
export function chunk<T>(list: readonly T[], size: number): T[][] {
  const out: T[][] = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < list.length; i += size) out.push(list.slice(i, i + size));
  return out;
}

/** One request (plan 2.4): the batch's rows with the changing items shown as
 *  their own values (the ones staff accepted by checking the row), the checked
 *  items, and for each item every key as the dialog showed the landlord's
 *  value (null for blank). */
export function applyRequestBody(
  rows: readonly ApplyRow[],
  items: readonly RequirementItemId[],
  landlord: Contact,
): ApplyRequirementsBody {
  const expected: Partial<Record<RequirementItemId, ItemValue>> = {};
  for (const id of items) expected[id] = landlordItemValue(landlord, id);
  return {
    units: rows.map((row) => ({ unitId: row.unitId, ownItems: [...row.own] })),
    items: [...items],
    expected,
  };
}

/** Plan 1.1: the plain words for each skip reason. A Map, so an inherited name
 *  such as `toString` never matches. */
const SKIP_REASON_COPY: ReadonlyMap<string, string> = new Map([
  ['changed_since_opened', 'changed since you opened this - review it again'],
  ['changed_during_apply', 'changed since you opened this - review it again'],
  ['already_matches', 'already matches'],
  ['landlord_changed', 'has a different landlord now'],
  ['deleted', 'was deleted'],
  ['not_found', 'no longer exists'],
]);
export function skipReasonCopy(reason: string): string {
  return SKIP_REASON_COPY.get(reason) ?? reason.replace(/_/g, ' ');
}

/** What the landlord page shows when an Apply finishes (D8). */
export interface ApplyDoneSummary {
  updated: number;
  skipped: Array<{ unitId: string; address: string; reason: string }>;
}

/** A property's address, else its id (the done message's `<address>`). */
export function unitAddress(unit: UnitItem | undefined, unitId: string): string {
  return (unit !== undefined ? formatAddress(unit.address) : '') || unitId;
}

/** The property's label exactly as the landlord page's Properties card shows
 *  it - "address - NBR" when the bedrooms are known (LandlordFile renders its
 *  rows through this, Task 6.8). The Apply dialog's row checkbox is named by
 *  it, so a property reads the same on the page and in the dialog (planner
 *  ruling on accessible names). */
export function propertyRowLabel(unit: UnitItem): string {
  const beds = typeof unit.beds === 'number' ? ` - ${unit.beds}BR` : '';
  return `${unitAddress(unit, unit.unitId)}${beds}`;
}

/** Merge the batch responses; name each skipped property from the rows the
 *  dialog read. */
export function summarizeApply(results: readonly ApplyRequirementsResult[], units: readonly UnitItem[]): ApplyDoneSummary {
  const byId = new Map(units.map((unit) => [unit.unitId, unit]));
  return {
    updated: results.reduce((n, result) => n + result.updated.length, 0),
    skipped: results.flatMap((result) =>
      result.skipped.map((s) => ({
        unitId: s.unitId,
        address: unitAddress(byId.get(s.unitId), s.unitId),
        reason: skipReasonCopy(s.reason),
      })),
    ),
  };
}

/** "1 property" / "N properties". */
export function propertiesCount(n: number): string {
  return `${n} ${n === 1 ? 'property' : 'properties'}`;
}
/** Plan 1.1: `Update <N> properties` (`Update 1 property`). */
export function updateButtonLabel(n: number): string {
  return `Update ${propertiesCount(n)}`;
}
/** Plan 1.1: `Updated <N> properties` (`Updated 1 property`). */
export function doneHeadline(n: number): string {
  return `Updated ${propertiesCount(n)}`;
}
/** Plan 1.1, stopped mid-run (singular per CI-6). */
export function stoppedNotice(n: number): string {
  return `Updated ${propertiesCount(n)} before this stopped. Review the rest and press Update again.`;
}
/** Plan 1.1: the first request answered 409 requirements_changed. */
export const REQUIREMENTS_CHANGED_NOTICE =
  "This landlord's requirements changed. Review the updated list and press Update again.";
/** CI-5 (proposed): the first request failed any other way. */
export const APPLY_FAILED_NOTICE = "Couldn't update the properties. Review the list and press Update again.";
/** Plan 1.1: the dialog's load error. */
export const APPLY_LOAD_ERROR = "Couldn't load this landlord's properties.";
/** Plan 1.1: why Apply to properties is disabled. */
export const APPLY_NO_PROPERTIES_REASON = 'This landlord has no properties yet.';
```

```tsx
export function CardAction({
  children,
  onClick,
  label,
  disabled,
  describedBy,
}: {
  children: React.ReactNode;
  onClick: () => void;
  /** Accessible label when the text alone is ambiguous (e.g. "Edit"). */
  label?: string;
  /** Disabled with a reason: render the reason in the card and pass its id
   *  as `describedBy` (property requirements D8, Apply to properties). */
  disabled?: boolean;
  describedBy?: string;
}): React.JSX.Element {
  return (
    <button
      type="button"
      className={styles.asideBtn}
      onClick={onClick}
      {...(label !== undefined && { 'aria-label': label })}
      {...(disabled === true && { disabled: true })}
      {...(describedBy !== undefined && { 'aria-describedby': describedBy })}
    >
      {children}
    </button>
  );
}
```

(b) Create `LandlordRequirementsCard.tsx`:

```tsx
// LandlordRequirementsCard - the landlord page's "Requirements /
// Qualifications" card (property requirements spec 2026-10-20, D9), right
// after Landlord onboarding: the landlord's eight requirement items in their
// groups, a blank item as the dashboard's blank marker. These are copy-only
// DEFAULTS (D5): a property gets them when it is created from this landlord, or
// when staff press Apply to properties - nothing on a property changes because
// this card changed. The last Apply's result shows here until the next Apply.
import { useId } from 'react';
import type { Contact } from '../../api/index.js';
import { BLANK, Card, CardAction } from './Card.js';
import {
  formatItemValue,
  isItemBlank,
  landlordItemValue,
  requirementItemsByGroup,
} from '../listing/requirements.js';
import { APPLY_NO_PROPERTIES_REASON, doneHeadline, type ApplyDoneSummary } from './applyRequirementsModel.js';
import styles from './LandlordRequirementsCard.module.css';

export interface LandlordRequirementsCardProps {
  contact: Contact;
  /** The landlord has at least one property of record (D8 disables Apply otherwise). */
  hasProperties: boolean;
  /** Opens "Apply to properties"; absent = no Apply action. */
  onApply?: () => void;
  /** Opens the landlord edit form. */
  onEdit?: () => void;
  /** The last Apply's result (D8 done message), or null. */
  notice?: ApplyDoneSummary | null;
}

export function LandlordRequirementsCard({
  contact,
  hasProperties,
  onApply,
  onEdit,
  notice,
}: LandlordRequirementsCardProps): React.JSX.Element {
  const reasonId = useId();
  const applyBlocked = onApply !== undefined && !hasProperties;
  const actions =
    onApply !== undefined || onEdit !== undefined ? (
      <>
        {onApply !== undefined ? (
          <CardAction onClick={onApply} disabled={!hasProperties} {...(applyBlocked && { describedBy: reasonId })}>
            Apply to properties
          </CardAction>
        ) : null}
        {onEdit !== undefined ? (
          <CardAction onClick={onEdit} label="Edit requirements">
            Edit
          </CardAction>
        ) : null}
      </>
    ) : undefined;

  return (
    <Card title="Requirements / Qualifications" aside={actions}>
      {applyBlocked ? (
        <p id={reasonId} className={styles.reason}>
          {APPLY_NO_PROPERTIES_REASON}
        </p>
      ) : null}
      {notice !== undefined && notice !== null ? (
        <div role="status" className={styles.notice}>
          <p className={styles.noticeLine}>{doneHeadline(notice.updated)}</p>
          {notice.skipped.length > 0 ? (
            <>
              <p className={styles.noticeLine}>{`${notice.skipped.length} skipped`}</p>
              <ul className={styles.skipped}>
                {notice.skipped.map((s) => (
                  <li key={s.unitId}>{`${s.address} - ${s.reason}`}</li>
                ))}
              </ul>
            </>
          ) : null}
        </div>
      ) : null}
      {requirementItemsByGroup().map(({ group, items }) => (
        <div key={group} className={styles.group}>
          <h4 className={styles.groupHeading}>{group}</h4>
          {items.map((item) => {
            const value = landlordItemValue(contact, item.id);
            return (
              <div key={item.id} role="group" aria-label={item.label} className={styles.item}>
                {items.length > 1 ? <span className={styles.itemLabel}>{item.label}</span> : null}
                <span className={styles.value}>{isItemBlank(value) ? BLANK : formatItemValue(item.id, value)}</span>
              </div>
            );
          })}
        </div>
      ))}
    </Card>
  );
}
```

### Task 6.9 - Landlord edit form: the Requirements / Qualifications fieldset

Goal: D9 - `ContactEditForm` gets a "Requirements / Qualifications" fieldset
for landlords, after Landlord onboarding, using the shared
`RequirementsFields` with audience 'landlord' (tags On property flyers / Staff
only, the landlord legend); it sends only the `req_` keys that changed, and on
the save that CHECKS One month's rent it sends `req_deposit: null` (D1). A
contact retyped away from landlord sends no `req_` key (the server 400s them,
plan 2.4). Uses S5's helpers exactly (ruling AR36,
`dashboard/src/routes/listing/requirementForm.ts`):
`requirementFormValuesFromLandlord(contact)` for the starting values,
`buildRequirementPatch(initial, current)` (`{ ok: true; patch } | { ok: false; error }`;
it already adds `deposit: null` on the save that checks One month's rent) and
`toLandlordPatch(patch)` (prefixes `req_`). An `ok: false` shows its `error` in
the form's error line and sends nothing - a DEFENSIVE branch with no UI test
(ruling PR2-1: the amount inputs' `min={0}` and the form's native validation
stop a bad amount before `onSubmit`; `ok: false` is pinned in S5 Task 5.3's
`requirementForm.test.ts`). A 400 `deposit_conflict` (ruling AR32)
shows `A deposit can be one month's rent or a fixed amount, not both. Reload the landlord and try again.`,
keeps the form open with what staff typed, and never falls through to the
generic save error. `RequirementsFields` renders no section heading (S5), so
the form renders the fieldset legend and `FlyerLegend` itself.

```tsx
    render(<ContactEditForm contact={WITH_REQUIREMENTS} onClose={vi.fn()} onSaved={vi.fn()} />);

    await waitFor(() => expect(updateContact).toHaveBeenCalled());
    const patch = updateContact.mock.calls[0]![1] as Record<string, unknown>;
```

### Task 6.11 - `ApplyRequirementsDialog`

Goal: D8 dialog B in full: re-read the landlord and its properties on open
(loading, error + Try again); left column "What to copy" (every item with the
landlord's value, filled items checked, blank items unchecked and marked
Clears); right column "Which properties" (address + status, live per-row
changes with own-value marks, Already matches, starting state, the hand
rules, no Select all); "Update N properties"; sequential batches of 100; a
mid-run 409 or failure stops, re-reads and says so; a first-request 409
`requirements_changed` re-reads and says so; on done, `onDone(summary)`.

Files:
- `dashboard/src/routes/contact/ApplyRequirementsDialog.tsx` (new)
- `dashboard/src/routes/contact/ApplyRequirementsDialog.module.css` (new)
- `dashboard/src/routes/contact/ApplyRequirementsDialog.test.tsx` (new)

Step 1 - tests. Create `ApplyRequirementsDialog.test.tsx`:

```tsx
import { render, screen, waitFor, within } from '@testing-library/react';
import userEvent from '@testing-library/user-event';
import { beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';
import { ApiError, type Contact, type UnitItem } from '../../api/index.js';

const getContact = vi.fn();
const getAllUnits = vi.fn();
const applyLandlordRequirements = vi.fn();
vi.mock('../../api/index.js', async () => {
  const actual = await vi.importActual<typeof import('../../api/index.js')>('../../api/index.js');
  return {
    ...actual,
    getContact: (...a: unknown[]) => getContact(...a),
    getAllUnits: (...a: unknown[]) => getAllUnits(...a),
    applyLandlordRequirements: (...a: unknown[]) => applyLandlordRequirements(...a),
  };
});

import { ApplyRequirementsDialog } from './ApplyRequirementsDialog.js';

const LANDLORD: Contact = {
  contactId: 'L1',
  type: 'landlord',
  firstName: 'James',
  lastName: 'Porter',
  req_no_pets: true,
  req_pet_fee: '$300',
  req_credit_requirements: '600+',
};
// beds: 3, so its row is named "1 Match St - 3BR" - the landlord Properties
// card's label (planner ruling on accessible names).
const MATCH: UnitItem = {
  unitId: 'u-match',
  landlordId: 'L1',
  status: 'available',
  address: { line1: '1 Match St' },
  beds: 3,
  no_pets: true,
  pet_fee: '$300',
  credit_requirements: '600+',
  requirement_sources: { pets: 'copied', credit_requirements: 'copied' },
};
const OLD: UnitItem = {
  unitId: 'u-old',
  landlordId: 'L1',
  status: 'occupied',
  address: { line1: '2 Old St' },
  no_pets: true,
  pet_fee: '$250',
  evictions_notes: 'Case by case',
  requirement_sources: { pets: 'copied' },
};
const OWN: UnitItem = {
  unitId: 'u-own',
  landlordId: 'L1',
  status: 'setup',
  address: { line1: '3 Own St' },
  pets: 'Cats OK',
  qualifications: 'Two references',
};
// Never listed: another landlord's property, and a deleted one.
const OTHER: UnitItem = { unitId: 'u-other', landlordId: 'L2', status: 'available', address: { line1: '9 Other St' } };
const DELETED: UnitItem = {
  unitId: 'u-deleted',
  landlordId: 'L1',
  status: 'available',
  address: { line1: '8 Deleted St' },
  deleted_at: '2026-06-01T00:00:00.000Z',
};

function many(n: number): UnitItem[] {
  return Array.from({ length: n }, (_, i): UnitItem => ({
    unitId: `u${i}`,
    landlordId: 'L1',
    status: 'available',
    address: { line1: `${i + 1} Many St` },
  }));
}

function renderDialog(): { onLandlordRead: ReturnType<typeof vi.fn>; onClose: ReturnType<typeof vi.fn>; onDone: ReturnType<typeof vi.fn> } {
  const handlers = { onLandlordRead: vi.fn(), onClose: vi.fn(), onDone: vi.fn() };
  render(<ApplyRequirementsDialog contactId="L1" {...handlers} />);
  return handlers;
}

/** The two columns, by the names the planner ruled: a group "What to copy"
 *  and a list "Which properties". */
async function columns(): Promise<{ copy: HTMLElement; which: HTMLElement }> {
  const dialog = await screen.findByRole('dialog', { name: 'Apply to properties' });
  const copy = await within(dialog).findByRole('group', { name: 'What to copy' });
  return { copy, which: within(dialog).getByRole('list', { name: 'Which properties' }) };
}
const rowBox = (which: HTMLElement, address: string): HTMLElement =>
  within(which).getByRole('checkbox', { name: address });
const row = (which: HTMLElement, address: string): HTMLElement => rowBox(which, address).closest('li') as HTMLElement;

beforeEach(() => {
  getContact.mockReset().mockResolvedValue(LANDLORD);
  getAllUnits.mockReset().mockResolvedValue([MATCH, OLD, OWN, OTHER, DELETED]);
  applyLandlordRequirements.mockReset();
});

describe('ApplyRequirementsDialog - reading', () => {
  it('re-reads the landlord and its properties on open, with a loading state, and hands the contact to the page', async () => {
    const { onLandlordRead } = renderDialog();
    expect(screen.getByText('Loading...')).toBeInTheDocument();
    await columns();
    expect(getContact).toHaveBeenCalledWith('L1', expect.any(AbortSignal));
    expect(getAllUnits).toHaveBeenCalledWith({ landlordId: 'L1' }, expect.any(AbortSignal));
    expect(onLandlordRead).toHaveBeenCalledWith(LANDLORD);
  });

  it('a failed landlord read shows the error with Try again, which reads both again', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    getContact.mockReset().mockRejectedValueOnce(new ApiError(500, 'boom', 'x')).mockResolvedValue(LANDLORD);
    renderDialog();
    expect(await screen.findByText("Couldn't load this landlord's properties.")).toBeInTheDocument();
    await user.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Try again' }));
    await columns();
    expect(getContact).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
    expect(getAllUnits).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
  });

  it('a failed properties read shows the same error', async () => {
    getAllUnits.mockReset().mockRejectedValue(new ApiError(503, 'unavailable', 'x'));
    renderDialog();
    expect(await screen.findByText("Couldn't load this landlord's properties.")).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Try again' })).toBeInTheDocument();
  });
});

describe('ApplyRequirementsDialog - the two columns', () => {
  it('What to copy: every item with the landlord value; filled items checked, blank ones unchecked and marked Clears', async () => {
    const { copy } = await columns();
    expect(within(copy).getAllByRole('checkbox')).toHaveLength(8);
    const pets = within(copy).getByRole('checkbox', { name: 'Pets' });
    expect(pets).toBeChecked();
    expect(pets).toHaveAccessibleDescription('No pets; pet fee $300');
    expect(within(copy).getByRole('checkbox', { name: 'Credit score' })).toBeChecked();
    for (const name of ['Evictions', 'Income requirements', 'Qualifications', 'Deposit', 'Application fee', 'Touring']) {
      const box = within(copy).getByRole('checkbox', { name });
      expect(box).not.toBeChecked();
      expect(box).toHaveAccessibleDescription('Clears');
      // "Clears" is visible text in the item's row.
      expect(box.closest('li')).toHaveTextContent('Clears');
    }
  });

  it('Which properties: changes per row, own values marked, Already matches, and the starting state', async () => {
    const { which } = await columns();
    // One listitem per property, each holding exactly one checkbox, named by
    // the landlord Properties card's label ("address - NBR" when beds are known).
    const items = within(which).getAllByRole('listitem');
    expect(items).toHaveLength(3);
    for (const li of items) expect(within(li).getAllByRole('checkbox')).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(rowBox(which, '1 Match St - 3BR')).toBeDisabled();
    expect(rowBox(which, '1 Match St - 3BR')).not.toBeChecked();
    expect(row(which, '1 Match St - 3BR')).toHaveTextContent('Already matches');
    expect(rowBox(which, '2 Old St')).toBeChecked();
    expect(row(which, '2 Old St')).toHaveTextContent('Credit score, Pets');
    expect(row(which, '2 Old St')).not.toHaveTextContent('own value');
    expect(row(which, '2 Old St')).toHaveTextContent('Occupied');
    expect(rowBox(which, '3 Own St')).not.toBeChecked();
    expect(row(which, '3 Own St')).toHaveTextContent('Credit score, Pets (own value)');
    expect(within(which).queryByRole('checkbox', { name: '9 Other St' })).toBeNull();
    expect(within(which).queryByRole('checkbox', { name: '8 Deleted St' })).toBeNull();
    expect(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Update 1 property' })).toBeEnabled();
    // There is no Select all.
    expect(screen.queryByRole('button', { name: /select all/i })).toBeNull();
    expect(screen.queryByRole('checkbox', { name: /select all/i })).toBeNull();
  });

  it('an all-blank landlord: checking a Clears item marks existing values as own values', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    getContact.mockReset().mockResolvedValue({ contactId: 'L1', type: 'landlord' } as Contact);
    getAllUnits.mockReset().mockResolvedValue([OWN]);
    renderDialog();
    const { copy, which } = await columns();
    expect(row(which, '3 Own St')).toHaveTextContent('Already matches');
    expect(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Update 0 properties' })).toBeDisabled();
    await user.click(within(copy).getByRole('checkbox', { name: 'Pets' }));
    expect(row(which, '3 Own St')).toHaveTextContent('Pets (own value)');
    expect(rowBox(which, '3 Own St')).not.toBeChecked();
  });

  it('unchecking an item recomputes every row: a row whose only own value was in it starts checked', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    renderDialog();
    const { copy, which } = await columns();
    await user.click(within(copy).getByRole('checkbox', { name: 'Pets' }));
    expect(rowBox(which, '3 Own St')).toBeChecked();
    expect(row(which, '3 Own St')).toHaveTextContent('Credit score');
    expect(row(which, '3 Own St')).not.toHaveTextContent('own value');
    expect(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Update 2 properties' })).toBeEnabled();
  });

  it('a hand-unchecked row stays unchecked until it becomes Already matches', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    renderDialog();
    const { copy, which } = await columns();
    await user.click(rowBox(which, '2 Old St'));
    expect(rowBox(which, '2 Old St')).not.toBeChecked();
    await user.click(within(copy).getByRole('checkbox', { name: 'Pets' }));
    expect(rowBox(which, '2 Old St')).not.toBeChecked(); // still has the credit change
    await user.click(within(copy).getByRole('checkbox', { name: 'Credit score' }));
    expect(row(which, '2 Old St')).toHaveTextContent('Already matches');
    await user.click(within(copy).getByRole('checkbox', { name: 'Credit score' }));
    expect(rowBox(which, '2 Old St')).toBeChecked(); // released: back to its starting state
  });

  it('a hand-checked row resets only when a left-column change ADDS an own value to it', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    renderDialog();
    const { copy, which } = await columns();
    await user.click(rowBox(which, '3 Own St'));
    expect(rowBox(which, '3 Own St')).toBeChecked();
    expect(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Update 2 properties' })).toBeEnabled();
    // Removing an item never resets it.
    await user.click(within(copy).getByRole('checkbox', { name: 'Credit score' }));
    expect(rowBox(which, '3 Own St')).toBeChecked();
    // Adding an item that is an own value here resets it: staff confirm again.
    await user.click(within(copy).getByRole('checkbox', { name: 'Qualifications' }));
    expect(rowBox(which, '3 Own St')).not.toBeChecked();
    expect(row(which, '3 Own St')).toHaveTextContent('Pets (own value), Qualifications (own value)');
  });
});

describe('ApplyRequirementsDialog - Update', () => {
  it('sends the checked rows with their own values, the checked items and the landlord values; done hands the summary to the page', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    applyLandlordRequirements.mockResolvedValue({
      updated: ['u-old'],
      skipped: [{ unitId: 'u-own', reason: 'changed_since_opened' }],
    });
    const { onDone } = renderDialog();
    const { which } = await columns();
    await user.click(rowBox(which, '3 Own St'));
    await user.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Update 2 properties' }));
    await waitFor(() =>
      expect(onDone).toHaveBeenCalledWith({

    expect(applyLandlordRequirements).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    expect(applyLandlordRequirements).toHaveBeenCalledWith('L1', {
      units: [
        { unitId: 'u-old', ownItems: [] },
        { unitId: 'u-own', ownItems: ['pets'] },

      items: ['credit_requirements', 'pets'],

        credit_requirements: { credit_requirements: '600+' },
        pets: { no_pets: true, pets: null, pet_fee: '$300' },

  it('sends more than 100 properties in batches of 100, one after another', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    const units = many(150);
    getAllUnits.mockReset().mockResolvedValue(units);
    let releaseFirst: (value: unknown) => void = () => undefined;
    applyLandlordRequirements
      .mockImplementationOnce(
        () =>
          new Promise((resolve) => {
            releaseFirst = resolve;
          }),
      )
      .mockResolvedValueOnce({ updated: units.slice(100).map((u) => u.unitId), skipped: [] });
    const { onDone } = renderDialog();
    await columns();
    await user.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Update 150 properties' }));
    await waitFor(() => expect(applyLandlordRequirements).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1));
    expect(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Update 150 properties' })).toBeDisabled();
    releaseFirst({ updated: units.slice(0, 100).map((u) => u.unitId), skipped: [] });
    await waitFor(() => expect(onDone).toHaveBeenCalledWith({ updated: 150, skipped: [] }));
    expect(applyLandlordRequirements).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
    const sizes = applyLandlordRequirements.mock.calls.map((c) => (c[1] as { units: unknown[] }).units.length);
    expect(sizes).toEqual([100, 50]);
  });

  it.each<[string, Error]>([
    ['answers 409', new ApiError(409, 'requirements_changed', 'x', { error: 'requirements_changed' })],
    ['fails', new TypeError('Failed to fetch')],
  ])('a later request that %s stops the run, re-reads and says how many landed', async (_label, failure) => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    const units = many(250);
    getAllUnits.mockReset().mockResolvedValue(units);
    applyLandlordRequirements
      .mockResolvedValueOnce({ updated: units.slice(0, 100).map((u) => u.unitId), skipped: [] })
      .mockRejectedValueOnce(failure);
    const { onDone, onClose } = renderDialog();
    await columns();
    await user.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Update 250 properties' }));
    expect(
      await screen.findByText('Updated 100 properties before this stopped. Review the rest and press Update again.'),
    ).toBeInTheDocument();
    await waitFor(() => expect(getContact).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2));
    expect(getAllUnits).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
    expect(applyLandlordRequirements).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2); // no third batch
    expect(onDone).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    // Closing now: the page re-reads its properties (some were written).
    await columns();
    await user.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Cancel' }));
    expect(onClose).toHaveBeenCalledWith(true);
  });

  it('a first request answering 409 requirements_changed re-reads and asks for another look', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    applyLandlordRequirements.mockRejectedValueOnce(
      new ApiError(409, 'requirements_changed', 'x', { error: 'requirements_changed' }),
    );
    getContact.mockReset().mockResolvedValueOnce(LANDLORD).mockResolvedValue({ ...LANDLORD, req_pet_fee: '$350' });
    const { onLandlordRead } = renderDialog();
    await columns();
    await user.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Update 1 property' }));
    expect(
      await screen.findByText("This landlord's requirements changed. Review the updated list and press Update again."),
    ).toBeInTheDocument();
    const { copy } = await columns();
    await waitFor(() =>
      expect(within(copy).getByRole('checkbox', { name: 'Pets' })).toHaveAccessibleDescription('No pets; pet fee $350'),
    );
    expect(onLandlordRead).toHaveBeenLastCalledWith({ ...LANDLORD, req_pet_fee: '$350' });
  });

  it('a first request failing any other way re-reads and says so (CI-5)', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    applyLandlordRequirements.mockRejectedValueOnce(new ApiError(500, 'boom', 'x'));
    renderDialog();
    await columns();
    await user.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Update 1 property' }));
    expect(
      await screen.findByText("Couldn't update the properties. Review the list and press Update again."),
    ).toBeInTheDocument();
    await waitFor(() => expect(getContact).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2));
  });

  it('Cancel before any Update closes without asking the page to re-read', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    const { onClose } = renderDialog();
    await columns();
    await user.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Cancel' }));
    expect(onClose).toHaveBeenCalledWith(false);
  });
});
```

Step 3 - implementation. Create `ApplyRequirementsDialog.tsx`:

```tsx
// ApplyRequirementsDialog - "Apply to properties" (property requirements spec
// 2026-10-20, D8 dialog B). Opening it RE-READS the landlord contact and the
// landlord's properties (the landlord page may have been open for hours), with
// a loading state and, if either read fails, an error with Try again.
//
// LEFT, "What to copy": every item with the landlord's value; items with a
// value start checked, blank ones unchecked and marked "Clears" (checking one
// copies the blank, clearing that item). RIGHT, "Which properties": the
// landlord's properties, each listing - live - the checked items that would
// CHANGE on it, marking the ones that are an OWN VALUE there (D6). A row with
// no changes reads "Already matches" and cannot be checked; a row with an own
// value starts unchecked; any other starts checked. No Select all. The hand
// rules and every other rule live in applyRequirementsModel.ts.
//
// Update sends the checked rows in batches of 100, one after another. A first
// request answering 409 requirements_changed (or failing) re-reads and asks
// for another look; a LATER one that answers 409 or fails stops the run,
// re-reads and says how many landed. When every batch lands the page gets the
// summary (onDone) and closes the dialog.
import { useEffect, useId, useRef, useState } from 'react';
import {
  ApiError,
  applyLandlordRequirements,
  getAllUnits,
  getContact,
  type ApplyRequirementsResult,
  type Contact,
  type UnitItem,
} from '../../api/index.js';
import { Button, StatusBadge } from '../../ui/index.js';
import {
  REQUIREMENT_ITEMS,
  formatItemValue,
  isItemBlank,
  landlordItemValue,
  type RequirementItemId,
} from '../listing/requirements.js';
import {
  APPLY_BATCH_SIZE,
  APPLY_FAILED_NOTICE,
  APPLY_LOAD_ERROR,
  APPLY_NO_PROPERTIES_REASON,
  REQUIREMENTS_CHANGED_NOTICE,
  applyRequestBody,
  applyRows,
  carryHandChoices,
  chunk,
  defaultCheckedItems,
  orderedItems,
  propertyRowLabel,
  rowIsChecked,
  stoppedNotice,
  summarizeApply,
  updateButtonLabel,
  type ApplyDoneSummary,
  type ApplyRow,
  type HandChoices,
} from './applyRequirementsModel.js';
import { Modal } from './Modal.js';
import styles from './ApplyRequirementsDialog.module.css';

export interface ApplyRequirementsDialogProps {
  contactId: string;
  /** Every landlord contact the dialog reads (open, Try again, a re-read after
   *  a 409 or a stop): the page takes it, so at close it holds the last one. */
  onLandlordRead: (contact: Contact) => void;
  /** Closed without finishing. `wrote` = an Update was sent from this dialog,
   *  so properties may have changed and the page re-reads them. */
  onClose: (wrote: boolean) => void;
  /** Every batch landed: the page re-reads its properties and shows the summary. */
  onDone: (summary: ApplyDoneSummary) => void;
}

type DialogLoad =
  | { phase: 'loading' }
  | { phase: 'error' }
  | { phase: 'ready'; landlord: Contact; units: UnitItem[] };

const ITEM_LABEL: ReadonlyMap<RequirementItemId, string> = new Map(REQUIREMENT_ITEMS.map((item) => [item.id, item.label]));

const isDeleted = (unit: UnitItem): boolean => typeof unit.deleted_at === 'string' && unit.deleted_at.length > 0;

export function ApplyRequirementsDialog({
  contactId,
  onLandlordRead,
  onClose,
  onDone,
}: ApplyRequirementsDialogProps): React.JSX.Element {
  const baseId = useId();
  const [load, setLoad] = useState<DialogLoad>({ phase: 'loading' });
  const [loadNonce, setLoadNonce] = useState(0);
  const [checkedItems, setCheckedItems] = useState<ReadonlySet<RequirementItemId>>(() => new Set());
  const [hand, setHand] = useState<HandChoices>(() => new Map());
  const [notice, setNotice] = useState<string | null>(null);
  const [sending, setSending] = useState(false);

  // The latest callbacks (the Modal.tsx onCloseRef precedent): the read effect
  // must not re-run because the page re-rendered with new inline handlers.
  const onLandlordReadRef = useRef(onLandlordRead);
  const onCloseRef = useRef(onClose);
  const onDoneRef = useRef(onDone);
  useEffect(() => {
    onLandlordReadRef.current = onLandlordRead;
    onCloseRef.current = onClose;
    onDoneRef.current = onDone;
  }, [onLandlordRead, onClose, onDone]);
  // True once an Update was sent: the server may have written even when the
  // answer was lost, so a later close asks the page to re-read.
  const attemptedRef = useRef(false);
  // False after unmount: an answer that lands later must not touch the page.
  const liveRef = useRef(true);
  useEffect(() => {
    liveRef.current = true;
    return () => {
      liveRef.current = false;
    };
  }, []);

  useEffect(() => {
    const controller = new AbortController();
    void (async () => {
      try {
        const [landlord, units] = await Promise.all([
          getContact(contactId, controller.signal),
          getAllUnits({ landlordId: contactId }, controller.signal),
        ]);
        if (controller.signal.aborted) return;
        setCheckedItems(defaultCheckedItems(landlord));
        setHand(new Map());
        // The landlord of record only, never a deleted property (D8) - the
        // server read already narrows both; this keeps the rule here too.
        setLoad({
          phase: 'ready',
          landlord,
          units: units.filter((u) => u.landlordId === contactId && !isDeleted(u)),
        });
        onLandlordReadRef.current(landlord);
      } catch (err) {
        if (controller.signal.aborted || (err instanceof DOMException && err.name === 'AbortError')) return;
        setLoad({ phase: 'error' });
      }
    })();
    return () => controller.abort();
  }, [contactId, loadNonce]);

  /** Read both again (Try again, and after a 409 or a stopped run). */
  const reload = (): void => {
    setLoad({ phase: 'loading' });
    setLoadNonce((n) => n + 1);
  };

  const ready = load.phase === 'ready' ? load : null;
  const rows: ApplyRow[] = ready !== null ? applyRows(ready.units, ready.landlord, checkedItems) : [];
  const checkedRows = rows.filter((r) => rowIsChecked(r, hand));
  const unitsById = new Map((ready?.units ?? []).map((u) => [u.unitId, u]));

  const toggleItem = (id: RequirementItemId): void => {
    if (ready === null || sending) return;
    const next = new Set(checkedItems);
    if (next.has(id)) next.delete(id);
    else next.add(id);
    setHand(carryHandChoices(hand, rows, applyRows(ready.units, ready.landlord, next)));
    setCheckedItems(next);
  };

  const toggleRow = (row: ApplyRow): void => {
    if (sending || row.alreadyMatches) return;
    const next = new Map(hand);
    next.set(row.unitId, !rowIsChecked(row, hand));
    setHand(next);
  };

  const close = (): void => {
    if (!sending) onCloseRef.current(attemptedRef.current);
  };

  const onUpdate = async (): Promise<void> => {
    if (ready === null || sending || checkedRows.length === 0) return;
    const { landlord, units } = ready;
    const items = orderedItems(checkedItems);
    const results: ApplyRequirementsResult[] = [];
    setSending(true);
    setNotice(null);
    attemptedRef.current = true;
    for (const [index, batch] of chunk(checkedRows, APPLY_BATCH_SIZE).entries()) {
      try {
        results.push(await applyLandlordRequirements(contactId, applyRequestBody(batch, items, landlord)));
      } catch (err) {
        if (!liveRef.current) return;
        setSending(false);
        if (index > 0) setNotice(stoppedNotice(summarizeApply(results, units).updated));
        else if (err instanceof ApiError && err.status === 409 && err.code === 'requirements_changed') {
          setNotice(REQUIREMENTS_CHANGED_NOTICE);
        } else setNotice(APPLY_FAILED_NOTICE);
        reload();
        return;
      }
    }
    if (!liveRef.current) return;
    setSending(false);
    onDoneRef.current(summarizeApply(results, units));
  };

  const whichHeadingId = `${baseId}-which`;

  return (
    <Modal
      title="Apply to properties"
      variant="wide"
      onClose={close}
      footer={
        <>
          <Button variant="secondary" size="sm" type="button" onClick={close} disabled={sending}>
            Cancel
          </Button>
          <Button
            variant="primary"
            size="sm"
            type="button"
            onClick={() => void onUpdate()}
            disabled={ready === null || sending || checkedRows.length === 0}
          >
            {updateButtonLabel(checkedRows.length)}
          </Button>
        </>
      }
    >
      {notice !== null ? (
        <p role="alert" className={styles.notice}>
          {notice}
        </p>
      ) : null}
      {load.phase === 'loading' ? (
        <p className={styles.muted}>Loading...</p>
      ) : load.phase === 'error' ? (
        <div role="alert" className={styles.loadError}>
          <p>{APPLY_LOAD_ERROR}</p>
          <Button variant="secondary" size="sm" type="button" onClick={reload}>
            Try again
          </Button>
        </div>
      ) : (
        <div className={styles.columns}>
          {/* Planner ruling (accessible names): the left column is a GROUP
              named "What to copy", one checkbox per item named by the item
              label; the right column is a LIST named "Which properties", one
              listitem per property holding exactly one checkbox named by the
              property's label as the landlord page's Properties card shows it. */}
          <fieldset className={styles.column}>
            <legend className={styles.columnHeading}>What to copy</legend>
            <ul className={styles.list}>
              {REQUIREMENT_ITEMS.map((item) => {
                const value = landlordItemValue(load.landlord, item.id);
                const valueId = `${baseId}-item-${item.id}`;
                return (
                  <li key={item.id} className={styles.row}>
                    <label className={styles.check}>
                      <input
                        type="checkbox"
                        checked={checkedItems.has(item.id)}
                        onChange={() => toggleItem(item.id)}
                        disabled={sending}
                        aria-describedby={valueId}
                      />
                      <span>{item.label}</span>
                    </label>
                    <span id={valueId} className={styles.detail}>
                      {isItemBlank(value) ? (
                        <span className={styles.clears}>Clears</span>
                      ) : (
                        formatItemValue(item.id, value)
                      )}
                    </span>
                  </li>
                );
              })}
            </ul>
          </fieldset>
          <div className={styles.column}>
            <h3 id={whichHeadingId} className={styles.columnHeading}>
              Which properties
            </h3>
            {rows.length === 0 ? (
              <p className={styles.muted}>{APPLY_NO_PROPERTIES_REASON}</p>
            ) : (
              <ul aria-labelledby={whichHeadingId} className={styles.list}>
                {rows.map((row, index) => {
                  const unit = unitsById.get(row.unitId);
                  const changesId = `${baseId}-row-${index}`;
                  return (
                    <li key={row.unitId} className={styles.row}>
                      <label className={styles.check}>
                        <input
                          type="checkbox"
                          checked={rowIsChecked(row, hand)}
                          onChange={() => toggleRow(row)}
                          disabled={row.alreadyMatches || sending}
                          aria-describedby={changesId}
                        />
                        <span>{unit !== undefined ? propertyRowLabel(unit) : row.unitId}</span>
                      </label>
                      {unit !== undefined ? <StatusBadge kind="listing" status={unit.status} /> : null}
                      <p id={changesId} className={styles.detail}>
                        {row.alreadyMatches
                          ? 'Already matches'
                          : row.changes.map((id, i) => (
                              <span key={id}>
                                {i > 0 ? ', ' : ''}
                                {ITEM_LABEL.get(id) ?? id}
                                {row.own.includes(id) ? <span className={styles.ownMark}> (own value)</span> : null}
                              </span>
                            ))}
                      </p>
                    </li>
                  );
                })}
              </ul>
            )}
          </div>
        </div>
      )}
    </Modal>
  );
}
```

Create `ApplyRequirementsDialog.module.css`:

```css
/* ApplyRequirementsDialog - "Apply to properties" (property requirements D8,
 * dialog B). Two columns on a wide screen (the Modal's wide variant), one
 * below 860px - the breakpoint the other dialogs use. Tokens only. */

.notice {
  margin: 0 0 var(--sp-3);
  padding: var(--sp-2) var(--sp-3);
  border: 1px solid var(--c-evt-amber-border);
  border-radius: var(--radius-sm);
  background: var(--c-evt-amber-bg);
  color: var(--c-evt-amber-text);
  font-size: var(--fs-sm);
}

.muted {
  margin: 0;
  font-size: var(--fs-sm);
  color: var(--c-text-muted);
}

.loadError {
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  align-items: flex-start;
  gap: var(--sp-2);
  font-size: var(--fs-sm);
  color: var(--c-danger);
}

.loadError p {
  margin: 0;
}

.columns {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr) minmax(0, 1.4fr);
  gap: var(--sp-4);
}

@media (max-width: 860px) {
  .columns {
    grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr);
  }
}

/* The left column is a <fieldset> (its legend names the group); reset the
 * browser frame so both columns look alike. */
.column {
  min-width: 0;
  margin: 0;
  padding: 0;
  border: 0;
}

.columnHeading {
  padding: 0;
  margin: 0 0 var(--sp-2);
  font-size: var(--fs-xs);
  font-weight: var(--fw-semibold);
  letter-spacing: 0.04em;
  text-transform: uppercase;
  color: var(--c-text-muted);
}

.list {
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  gap: var(--sp-2);
  margin: 0;
  padding: 0;
  list-style: none;
}

.row {
  display: flex;
  flex-wrap: wrap;
  align-items: baseline;
  gap: var(--sp-1) var(--sp-2);
  font-size: var(--fs-sm);
}

.check {
  display: inline-flex;
  align-items: baseline;
  gap: var(--sp-2);
  min-width: 0;
  color: var(--c-text);
  font-weight: var(--fw-medium);
  overflow-wrap: anywhere;
}

/* The landlord value under an item, or a property's changes - indented to sit
 * under the label, past the checkbox. */
.detail {
  flex-basis: 100%;
  margin: 0;
  padding-left: 1.5rem;
  color: var(--c-text-muted);
  white-space: pre-line;
  overflow-wrap: anywhere;
}

.clears {
  font-weight: var(--fw-semibold);
  color: var(--c-warning);
}

.ownMark {
  font-weight: var(--fw-semibold);
  color: var(--c-pill-partner-bg);
}
```

### Task 6.12 - Wiring: the landlord page opens the dialog, re-reads and shows the result

```tsx
describe('ContactDetail - Apply to properties (property requirements D8)', () => {
  it('opens from the Requirements card; on done re-reads the properties, takes the last-read landlord and shows the result', async () => {
    const { default: userEvent } = await import('@testing-library/user-event');
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    getContact.mockResolvedValue(LANDLORD);
    applyLandlordRequirements.mockReset().mockResolvedValue({ updated: ['u1'], skipped: [] });
    renderAt('L1');
    const apply = await screen.findByRole('button', { name: 'Apply to properties' });
    // The dialog's re-read finds requirements recorded since the page loaded.
    getContact.mockResolvedValue({ ...LANDLORD, req_pet_fee: '$300' });
    const unitReadsBefore = getAllUnits.mock.calls.length;

    await user.click(apply);
    const dialog = await screen.findByRole('dialog', { name: 'Apply to properties' });
    expect(getAllUnits).toHaveBeenCalledWith({ landlordId: 'L1' }, expect.anything());
    // The row reads as the Properties card does ("1450 Joseph Blvd - 2BR").
    const which = await within(dialog).findByRole('list', { name: 'Which properties' });
    expect(within(which).getByRole('checkbox', { name: '1450 Joseph Blvd - 2BR' })).toBeChecked();
    await user.click(within(dialog).getByRole('button', { name: 'Update 1 property' }));

    await waitFor(() => expect(screen.queryByRole('dialog', { name: 'Apply to properties' })).toBeNull());
    expect(applyLandlordRequirements).toHaveBeenCalledWith('L1', expect.objectContaining({ items: ['pets'] }));
    // The page re-read its properties (the existing refetch) on top of the dialog's read ...
    await waitFor(() => expect(getAllUnits.mock.calls.length).toBeGreaterThan(unitReadsBefore + 1));
    // ... took the landlord contact the dialog last read ...
    const card = screen
      .getByRole('heading', { name: /^Requirements \/ Qualifications/ })
      .closest('section') as HTMLElement;
    expect(within(card).getByText('pet fee $300')).toBeInTheDocument();
    // ... and says what happened.
    expect(within(card).getByRole('status')).toHaveTextContent('Updated 1 property');
  });

  it('Cancel before any Update closes the dialog and re-reads nothing', async () => {
    const { default: userEvent } = await import('@testing-library/user-event');
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    getContact.mockResolvedValue(LANDLORD);
    renderAt('L1');
    await user.click(await screen.findByRole('button', { name: 'Apply to properties' }));
    const dialog = await screen.findByRole('dialog', { name: 'Apply to properties' });
    await within(dialog).findByRole('group', { name: 'What to copy' });
    const unitReads = getAllUnits.mock.calls.length;
    await user.click(within(dialog).getByRole('button', { name: 'Cancel' }));
    await waitFor(() => expect(screen.queryByRole('dialog', { name: 'Apply to properties' })).toBeNull());
    expect(getAllUnits.mock.calls.length).toBe(unitReads);
    expect(screen.queryByText(/^Updated \d/)).toBeNull();
  });
});
```

## 1. CONTRACT ISSUES (for the planner's ruling)

**CI-1 (MED) - the Requirements cards' action names and headings are unbound,
and the obvious choices break existing selectors suite-wide.** Plan 1.1 binds
only visible text (`Card title Requirements / Qualifications; actions Apply to
properties, Edit`, plan :185-186; property card `Card titles Requirements`, plan
:175). Evidence of the collisions:
- The landlord page's Details card action is already
  `<CardAction onClick={onEdit} label="Edit contact details">`
  (`dashboard/src/routes/contact/LandlordFile.tsx:125`), and D9 says the new
  card's Edit "opens the existing landlord edit form". If S6 reuses that label,
  every `getByRole('button', { name: 'Edit contact details' })` on a landlord
  page (substring match; `e2e/scenarios/steps.ts:3925` `openEditDialog`, used by
  `teamRecordsContractSigned`, `teamRecordsLandlordOnboarding`,
  `teamRecordsApprovalCriteria`, `teamParksLead`, `setLandlordStatus`;
  `e2e/tests/dashboard-next/contact-detail.spec.ts:147`) becomes a strict-mode
  violation and `landlord-onboarding.spec.ts` dies.
- `Card` renders its `aside` INSIDE the `<h3>` (`dashboard/src/routes/contact/Card.tsx:20-30`),
  so an action's aria-label joins the card heading's accessible name. Existing
  substring heading selectors on these pages: `getByRole('heading', { name: 'Details' })`
  on a landlord page (`steps.ts:1477-1479`, `expectLeadInterested`),
  `{ name: 'Notes' }` on the landlord page (`contact-detail.spec.ts:142`) and on
  the property page (`listing-activity.spec.ts:286`, a `section` filtered by it).
  A Requirements heading or nested heading whose name contains "details" or
  "notes" (an Edit aria-label such as "Edit requirement details", or field
  labels "Pets (details)" / "Evictions (details)" / "Deposit notes" rendered as
  h4) makes those resolve to two elements.
- Proposed ruling (binding for S6): landlord card actions are
  `Apply to properties` (no aria-label override; accessible name exactly that)
  and an Edit CardAction with `label="Edit requirements"`; the property card's
  Edit CardAction has `label="Edit property requirements"`. Inside either
  Requirements card no element is a heading (h1-h6) except the card title and
  the four group headings (`Screening`, `Pets`, `Move-in costs`, `Touring`);
  field labels render as plain text (the existing `KV` pattern,
  `Card.tsx:136-158`), never as headings.

**CI-2 (MED) - the Apply dialog's row structure is unbound, and the spec's E2E
scenario cannot address a row without it.** Plan 1.1 (:188-192) binds the dialog
title, column titles, marks (`Clears`, `own value`, `Already matches`) and the
button text, but no roles. D8 needs a per-property checkbox and per-row change
list; the e2e must read "row A unchecked, own value marked; row B checked".
Proposed ruling (binding for S6): the dialog is the existing `Modal`
(`dashboard/src/routes/contact/Modal.tsx:170-172`, named by its title
`Apply to properties`); the right column is a `<ul>` whose accessible name is
`Which properties` (`aria-labelledby` its column heading); one `<li>` per
property, holding exactly ONE checkbox (accessible name starting with the
property's one-line address, so it contains the street line), the LABEL of
each changing item (`Evictions`, `Credit score`, `Income requirements`,
`Qualifications`, `Pets`, `Deposit`, `Application fee`, `Touring`) as text, the
text `own value` beside each own-value item (once per own-value item), and on
a no-change row the text `Already matches` with its checkbox disabled. The
submit button's accessible name is exactly `Update <N> properties` /
`Update 1 property` (no aria-label override). The done message on the landlord
page begins `Updated <N> properties`.

## 2. Facts the tasks rely on (verified)

Harness and runner:
- F1. One worker, no parallelism, no retries; per-test cap 60 s
  (`DEFAULT_TEST_TIMEOUT_MS`), expect timeout 15 s
  (`e2e/playwright.config.ts:115,135,140-143`). `test.slow()` triples the cap.
- F2. A single-file e2e run is `npm run e2e -w @housingchoice/e2e -- <files>`
  (one npm hop into the workspace, whose script is `playwright test`,
  `e2e/package.json:7`); root `npm run e2e` is `npm run e2e -w @housingchoice/e2e`
  (`package.json:41`), a double hop that eats `--flags`. It still boots the
  hermetic stack (lane-isolated, never :5174/:8080).
- F3. `reuseExistingServer` adopts a same-commit stack on a commit match alone
  (AGENTS.md); an uncommitted mutation therefore needs a COLD boot, and a stack
  left running by a mutated run must be gone before the next run.
- F4. `Modal` is `role="dialog"` named by its title (`dashboard/src/routes/contact/Modal.tsx:170-172`).
  `Card` is a `<section>` whose `<h3>` holds the title AND the aside action
  (`Card.tsx:20-30`); `CardAction` sets `aria-label` from `label` (`Card.tsx:34-54`);
  `KV` is `<div><span>k</span><span>v</span></div>` (`Card.tsx:136-158`).
- F5. The flyer renders each fact as a `<dt>`/`<dd>` pair inside one `<dl>`
  (`dashboard/src/routes/public/FlyerPage.tsx:278-337`); dollar values are
  `$${n}` with no thousands separator (`:301,307`); the voucher line is
  `Fits a <strong>N-bedroom</strong> voucher` (`:267`).
- F6. Tour type labels: `landlord_led` -> `Landlord-led` (`dashboard/src/api/types.ts:907-909`).
- F7. `UnitCreateForm`: address inputs are named by sr-only labels `Street address`,
